# Architecture

Owner: the architect subagent. The main session reads this and never edits it; the contract guard enforces it (`.claude/hooks/protected.json`). If something here is wrong or missing, escalate to the architect (`docs/build/RECOVERY.md` rung d).
Brief references (§n) point to `brief/BRIEF.md`.

---

## A. Design system (approved by Brian, Oct 5 2026)

### A1. Color tokens (`src/styles/tokens.css`)

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `--green-900` | `#0C3F35` | Default page background: header, hero, Book page, footer; (step V) both rate cards' fill (as `--bg-dark`) |
| `--green-700` | `#125245` | Secondary dark surfaces; link color on cream |
| `--green-300` | `#7FA396` | Hairlines and borders on dark, including the scrolled header's hairline (M2, §A3 eighth motion exception) and the event notice box's border on the green band (E4, §B10). **Not text** (4.26:1) |
| `--terra-500` | `#C37A5B` | Logo, the H1 resistor divider (8A), focus ring, both rate cards' top edge, title rule and icons (step V), the dropdown Ω marker (step V, `Dropdown`), large display text only (3.0:1 on cream, 3.5:1 on green-900) |
| `--terra-700` | `#9C5739` | CTA button fill (cream text, 4.89:1); any small terracotta text |
| `--cream` | `#F3F2F0` | Text on dark; background of reading bands |
| `--ink` | `#0B2620` | Body text on cream (14.3:1) |
| `--line-dark` / `--line-light` | cream 15% / ink 12% | Dividers |
| `--shadow-lift` | `0 6px 16px` ink 18% | (E10, I-102) the only shadow on the site: an event credit on hover and keyboard focus (§A3 fourteenth exception). Not a colour pair, so not in `check:contrast` |
| `--bodymap-figure` | `#D3D7DC` | (B0, I-073, §B12) the body map figure's grey: the art's silhouette fill, measured from the delivered SVGs Nov 10, 2026; B1's art test pins them equal. Background only, never text |
| `--pin-pain` · `--pin-discomfort` · `--pin-injury` · `--pin-numb` · `--pin-avoid` | `--terra-700` · `--terra-500` · `--green-700` · `--ink` · `--ink` (stroke on cream) | (B0, §B12) body map pin fills; shape is the main difference (circle, diamond, triangle, 4-point star, ring with slash), colour backs it up (BM-3). B1 adds `check:contrast` rules: each fill at least 3:1 against `--pin-halo`, `--pin-edge` at least 3:1 against `--bodymap-figure` |
| `--pin-halo` / `--pin-edge` | `--cream` / `--ink` | (B0, §B12) every pin's 3px halo ring and 1px edge, so pins show on the grey figure |

Use the semantic aliases (`--bg-dark`, `--text-on-light`, `--cta-bg`, …) in components. **No raw hex values outside `tokens.css`.**

Contrast (verified):
- cream on green-700 is 8.1:1
- cream on green-900 is 10.6:1
- ink on cream is 14.3:1

### A2. Typography
- **Text:** DM Sans, variable 400–700.
- **Display:** Saira Semi Condensed 700, set uppercase with `letter-spacing: 0.01em`. Used **only** for H1 and the home hero line.
- **Files:** self-hosted Latin-subset woff2 in `src/assets/fonts/`:
  - `dm-sans-latin-var.woff2`
  - `saira-semi-condensed-latin-700.woff2`

  `tokens.css` references them by relative URL, so Vite hashes them and applies the base path. Both fonts are OFL, from Google Fonts. There's no npm font package and no Google Fonts `<link>` at runtime.
- **Preload:** `Base.astro` preloads both fonts (`import url from '../assets/fonts/x.woff2?url'`).
- **Scale tokens:**
  - `--fs-small` 0.875rem
  - `--fs-body` 17→18px
  - `--fs-h3` 1.25rem
  - `--fs-h2` 1.6rem
  - `--fs-h1` clamp 2.4→4rem
- **Line height:** 1.55 for body, 1.05 for display. **Measure:** max 65ch.
- **Numerals:** rates, minutes and days use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.
- **Case:** sentence case everywhere except the display face.

### A3. Layout and restraint
- **Green-dominant.**
  - Header, home hero, Book page and footer are on `--green-900`.
  - Reading content (Services body, About text, home info blocks) sits in full-bleed **cream bands** with ink text.
  - No cards with shadows and no rounded blobs. The radius is 2px. Exceptions on event pages only (Brian, Nov 8, 2026): the credit hover shadow (`--shadow-lift`, fourteenth exception) and round timeline dots (E10, I-100, §B10 E8–E11).
- **The one memorable element** is the anatomical back illustration (`src/assets/graphic-green.png`), large and bleeding off the right or bottom edge of the home hero. Everywhere else stays quiet.
- **Terracotta** appears only in the logo, the CTA button fill, the divider under each H1, the map's north zone and pin, the focus ring, the dropdown marker (step V, §B3 `Dropdown`), the 404 page's Ω (M1, fifth motion exception), and on Pricing (step V, §B3 `PriceTable`) each rate card's top edge, title rule and icons (`--accent`); on event pages (E1, §B10) the timeline markers and each notice's top edge. No card is filled terracotta (step V, Brian, Oct 30 2026: the terracotta 90-minute card was dropped).
- **H1 divider (8A): a resistor symbol**, the ANSI/IEEE zigzag (lead, six alternating strokes, lead). It replaces the 3px × 48px rule, in `global.css` `h1::after`. It's drawn as a CSS mask over `background: var(--accent)`: an inline `data:image/svg+xml` with `viewBox="0 0 72 12"` and the path `M0 6H18L21 1L27 11L33 1L39 11L45 1L51 11L54 6H72`, `fill="none"`, `stroke="black"` (the mask only reads alpha; no hex), `stroke-width="2"`, `stroke-linejoin="miter"`. Size 72×12px. Set `mask` and `-webkit-mask`. Subtle: the same terracotta as before and a 2px stroke. **Spacing:** on every page with an H1, there's ≥ `--s-8` between the bottom of the zigzag and the next element. Use one global rule, not per-page margins. **Electricity pulse (step V; Brian, Oct 30 2026):** CSS only, no JS. The background is a `linear-gradient(90deg, ...)`: `var(--accent)` with `var(--text-on-dark)` as the bright band at the centre, sized `300% 100%` (three times the mask's width), resting at `background-position: 100% 0` so only accent shows. Keyframes `ohm-pulse` animate `background-position` from `100% 0` to `0 0`, so the band travels left to right and the mask limits it to the zigzag: 1.2s, `ease-in-out`, once on page load, `animation-delay: 0.3s`. `h1:hover::after` and `h1:active::after` play `ohm-pulse-hover` (same steps, a different name so the animation restarts), 1.2s, `ease-in-out`, once. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` there is no animation and the divider stays plain accent. **Hit area (Brian, step V):** `h1 { pointer-events: none }` and `h1::after { pointer-events: auto }`, so only the symbol answers hover and press, not the heading text (the `h1:hover::after` / `h1:active::after` selectors stay; hovering the pseudo-element counts as hovering the `h1`). Tokens only, no raw hex. Only `background-position` animates. Test: `tests/divider-pulse.test.ts`.
- **Never:**
  - eyebrow labels
  - numbered markers (unless the content is a real sequence)
  - entrance animations or scroll effects, except the numbered motion exceptions below (the fifth to tenth only within the motion rules; the eleventh to fifteenth on event pages only, within their own rules)
  - hover motion beyond a 150ms color or underline change, except the button settle (sixth exception) and the event credit lift (fourteenth)
  - loops (`infinite`) outside `/hello`
  - parallax on more than one layer, or on text
  - client JavaScript or a router for motion (no Astro `ClientRouter`, no `astro:transitions`)

  `prefers-reduced-motion` sets `--transition: 0ms`.
- **One exception (9A, revised 10A): the `/hello` entrance page** (§B8) has a light running along the Ω (one 3s lap, once; Brian, Nov 1 2026), fade-ins for the line and the `(Enter)` cue, and (F2, I-039) a slow breathing scale on the line `Take the path of least resistance` (`ohm-breathe`, §B8), at Brian's request; (step V trial; Brian, Oct 30 2026) the Ω breathes with it, in step (`transform` on the `.hello-mark` wrapper, which holds the Ω and the cue, Nov 1 2026, §B8), and (Brian, Nov 1 2026) a glow pulse lights the Ω on each inhale (`.omega-pulse`, §B8). **Second exception (step V; Brian, Oct 30 2026): the H1 divider's electricity pulse** (`ohm-pulse` once on load, `ohm-pulse-hover` on H1 hover and active; see the H1 divider bullet above). It overrides the Never list's entrance-animation and hover-motion items for this one element (the fifth to tenth exceptions below add the only other load, hover and scroll motion). `/hello` has no H1, so it is unaffected. **Third exception (step V; Brian, Oct 30 2026): the dropdown marker** (§B3 `Dropdown`): when a dropdown opens, its plus rotates and fades into the Ω (300ms, `transform` and `opacity` only), and back when it closes. It answers the open/close click, not hover or load. **Fourth exception (step V; Brian, Oct 30 2026): the Home logo spin** (§B3 `Header`, §B8 Motion note): on Home only, a plain click on the header logo turns its Ω once, counter-clockwise, about the Ω's own centre (`ohm-spin`, `rotate(0)` to `rotate(-360deg)`, 0.9s, `ease-in-out`; a flat 2D turn, no flip, no `perspective`) instead of reloading Home; the wordmark does not move (on phones the icon, which is the Ω alone, turns). It answers the click, not hover or load, and needs `src/scripts/logo-spin.ts`; on every other page the logo is a plain link and does not move (it only scales with the scroll-linked header, eighth exception). Nothing else on the site moves except the fifth to tenth exceptions below. Reduced motion turns all of it off (the Home logo then reloads Home as a plain link).
- **Motion set two (Brian approved Oct 30, 2026, step V era; built in M1 and M2): the fifth to tenth exceptions.** Brian's ideas 2, 3, 4, 7, 8 and 10.
  - **Motion rules** (bind these six; the first four exceptions keep their own specs):
    - **CSS only.** No client script, no library, no Astro `ClientRouter` / `astro:transitions` / `transition:*` directives. The client-script count stays fixed (§D; four since I-054). Reason: the zero-JS rule (BRIEF §3) and every page working with JS off.
    - **Properties:** only `translate`, `scale`, `transform`, `opacity`, and on the 404 Ω `stroke-dashoffset` (paint only, like `/hello`). No layout property animates; the header height and every box size stay fixed. CLS 0.
    - **Small distances:** entrance rise 8px, button lift 2px (3px at its overshoot), hero drift 16px, header logo scale 0.88.
    - **Short:** at most 700ms per motion (the page transition is 200ms). The earlier exceptions keep their durations.
    - **One-shot:** entrances play once per page load and never replay on scroll back. No loops (`infinite`) outside `/hello`.
    - **One parallax layer:** the Home hero art. Never text, never the map, never terrain (it must stay aligned with roads and zones on `/book`).
    - **Reduced motion:** every rule sits inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, so `reduce` gives the static design (the `--transition: 0ms` convention covers only the colour transitions).
    - **Progressive:** an element's resting style is its final, visible state, so content shows with JS off and in browsers without the feature. Scroll-linked rules (8, 10) sit inside `@supports (animation-timeline: scroll())`; the entrance (9) inside `@supports (animation-trigger: --t play-once)`. Write `animation-timeline` and `animation-trigger` after any `animation` shorthand (the shorthand resets the timeline).
    - Tokens only, no raw hex, no new token, no copy change. `/hello` gets none of them except the page transition when it navigates to Home.
  - **Browser support** (pinned Oct 30, 2026): cross-document view transitions Chrome/Edge 126+, Safari and iOS Safari 18.2+, Firefox partial (plain navigation) ([caniuse](https://caniuse.com/cross-document-view-transitions)); `animation-timeline: scroll()` Chrome/Edge 115+, Safari and iOS Safari 26+, Firefox listed from 159 ([caniuse](https://caniuse.com/mdn-css_properties_animation-timeline_scroll)); `animation-trigger` / `timeline-trigger` Chrome/Edge 146+ only, not Safari or Firefox ([caniuse](https://caniuse.com/mdn-css_properties_animation-trigger); [Chrome blog, Dec 12, 2025](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/scroll-triggered-animations); [MDN trigger-scope](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/trigger-scope), updated Oct 12, 2026: an animated element that is its own trigger finds it first). Checked by the architect on Oct 30, 2026 in Playwright's Chromium 156: a below-the-fold triggered item holds its `from` keyframe until it enters, plays once, and does not replay after scrolling to the top and back; a named `view-timeline` on an `overflow: hidden` hero and a `scroll(root block)` header animation both progress. Everyone else gets the static design.
  - **Fifth exception (M1): the 404 Ω trace.** `src/pages/404.astro`, inside the first section's container, above the H1: an inline `<svg class="nf-mark" viewBox={omega.viewBox} aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">` from `src/data/omega.json`, holding two paths with `d={omega.d}`: `.nf-mark__fill` (`fill: var(--accent)`) and on top `.nf-mark__line` (`pathLength="1"`, `fill: none`, `stroke: var(--accent)`, `stroke-width: 20` in viewBox units, about 2px on screen, `stroke-linejoin: round`, `stroke-dasharray: 1`; no `vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke`, for the reason in §B8). Size: `width: 4.5rem`, `height: auto`, `aspect-ratio` from the viewBox (as `/hello` does, so no CLS), `display: block`, `margin-bottom: var(--s-4)`. Motion, once on load, in the `/hello` lap language: the line draws from the right foot's inner corner, clockwise (`omega.d` starts there): `@keyframes ohm-trace` `stroke-dashoffset` 1 → 0, 700ms `ease-in-out`, delay 0.2s; then the fill settles in: `@keyframes ohm-trace-fill` `opacity` 0 → 1, 300ms `ease-out`, delay 0.9s. Both `animation-fill-mode: backwards`; the resting style is the end state (dashoffset 0, fill opacity 1), so reduced motion shows the filled Ω at once. No copy change, no script; the page stays `noindex`. Class names never start with `omega-` (`check:dist` reserves that string on Home). The H1 divider pulse runs as on every page.
  - **Sixth exception (M1): the button settle ("friction released").** `src/styles/global.css`, on `.btn` (BookCta, the header Book button, ContactButtons, the OfficeCard and ZoneCard booking buttons, ZonePicker's map-tinted area buttons, the Google Maps button, the policies Expand/Collapse buttons). All inside `@media (hover: hover) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`:
    ```css
    .btn        { transition: background-color var(--transition), border-color var(--transition), color var(--transition), translate 150ms ease; }
    .btn:hover  { translate: 0 -2px; animation: ohm-settle 260ms ease-out;
                  transition: background-color var(--transition), border-color var(--transition), color var(--transition); }
    .btn:active { translate: 0 0; animation: none;
                  transition: background-color var(--transition), border-color var(--transition), color var(--transition), translate 60ms ease-out; }
    @keyframes ohm-settle { 0% { translate: 0 0; } 60% { translate: 0 -3px; } 100% { translate: 0 -2px; } }
    ```
    Sequence: hover in → `ohm-settle` lifts 2px through a 1px overshoot (no translate transition on the way in, because a running transition would override the animation); press → back down in 60ms; release while still hovering → `ohm-settle` plays again (its name returns, so it restarts): the spring after friction; leave → back to rest over 150ms. The `translate` property, never `transform`, so it stacks with any transform. Colours keep their 150ms change. Not on touch-only devices (`hover: none`), keyboard focus, `.map-reset`, `.map-info`, dropdown summaries, nav text links or the logo. ZonePicker's `is-hot` (the linked hover from the map) does not lift. The `.btn` rules outside this block are unchanged.
  - **Seventh exception (M1): page transitions.** Native cross-document view transitions. `src/styles/global.css`:
    ```css
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
      @view-transition { navigation: auto; }
      ::view-transition-group(*), ::view-transition-old(*), ::view-transition-new(*) { animation-duration: 200ms; }
    }
    ```
    and in `src/components/Header.astro` `.site-header { view-transition-name: site-header; }`. The page cross-fades in 200ms (the browser's default fade); the header is its own layer and, being the same on both pages, stays visually still (from a page left scrolled, the logo eases back to full size within the 200ms). Same-origin only; reloads, address-bar and bookmark navigations don't transition ([Chrome docs](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/view-transitions/cross-document), read Oct 30, 2026). The `/hello` click pause navigates by script, which transitions; the header fades in with Home. No `<link rel="expect">` or `blocking="render"`. Browsers without support navigate plainly.
  - **Eighth exception (M2): the scroll-linked header.** `src/components/Header.astro`, inside `@supports (animation-timeline: scroll())` and `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, over the first 40px of page scroll (`animation-timeline: scroll(root block)`, `animation-range: 0px 40px`, `linear both`): `.site-header::after` (`content: ''`, `position: absolute`, `inset-inline: 0`, `bottom: -1px`, `height: 1px`, `background: var(--green-300)`, `pointer-events: none`) goes from `opacity: 0` to 1 (`ohm-header-line`), so the existing `--line-dark` hairline brightens; and `.site-header__logo` (the link, `transform-origin: left center`) goes from `scale: 1` to `scale: 0.88` (`ohm-header-logo`). **The header box stays `--header-h` and its padding never changes:** the header is sticky and in flow, so any height change would shift the page (CLS) and jump the scroll position; the "tighter" look is the logo scale. **No fight with the Home logo spin:** the scroll animation sets `scale` on the link; `ohm-spin` sets `transform` on `.logo-omega` / `.logo-icon` inside it, so the two compose. Never animate `.logo-omega`, `.logo-icon` or `transform` here. A page too short to scroll keeps the resting header.
  - **Ninth exception (M2): the content entrance.** `src/styles/global.css`, a `.rise` utility:
    ```css
    @keyframes ohm-rise { from { opacity: 0; translate: 0 8px; } }
    @supports (animation-trigger: --t play-once) {
      @media screen and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
        .rise { animation: ohm-rise 400ms ease-out both; animation-delay: calc(var(--rise-i, 0) * 60ms);
                timeline-trigger: --ohm-rise view(); animation-trigger: --ohm-rise play-once; }
        .rise:nth-of-type(2) { --rise-i: 1; }  .rise:nth-of-type(3) { --rise-i: 2; }  .rise:nth-of-type(n + 4) { --rise-i: 3; }
      }
    }
    ```
    Each item is its own trigger: it fades up 8px when it enters the viewport, once per page load, and never replays. Items already in view at load rise at once, 60ms apart in sibling order (capped at 180ms). `screen` keeps print static. **Uses (nine items, no others):** Home's three `.info > div` blocks (`index.astro`), Pricing's two `.rate-card`s (`PriceTable`), Services' four specialty `Dropdown`s (`rise` prop, §B3); from E10 (fifteenth exception) also the section containers of event pages after the hero. Never an H1, the hero, a page's first section, the header, the footer, `/book` or the map. **Screens:** `npm run shots` captures with reduced motion (a full-page capture never scrolls, so untriggered items would show blank).
  - **Tenth exception (M2): the Home hero drift (parallax).** `src/pages/index.astro`, inside `@supports (animation-timeline: scroll())` and `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`: `.hero { view-timeline: --ohm-hero block; }` and `.hero-art { animation: ohm-drift linear both; animation-timeline: --ohm-hero; animation-range: exit 0% exit 100%; }` with `@keyframes ohm-drift { from { translate: 0 0; } to { translate: 0 16px; } }`. As the hero scrolls away, the anatomy art falls 16px behind the text. The `translate` property, so the desktop `transform: translateY(-50%)` stays. Use the hero's named timeline, never an anonymous `view()` or `scroll()` on the art: `.hero { overflow: hidden }` makes the hero a scroll container, and those would bind to it and never progress. The hero's overflow clips the drift. Text, opacity, size and mask never change. `/hello` uses the same image and does not drift.
- **Motion set three, event pages only (Brian, Nov 8, 2026; I-095, I-098, I-099, I-102, I-105): the eleventh to fifteenth exceptions.** Specs in §B10 → E8–E11. Their rules (the fifth to tenth keep theirs):
  - **Started by script, moved by CSS.** Eleven to thirteen answer an RSVP or a click, so the existing RSVP client (`src/scripts/rsvp.ts`) adds an element or a class; every movement is a CSS `@keyframes` animation or transition. No library, no `element.animate()`, no `requestAnimationFrame` loop. Fourteen and fifteen are CSS only.
  - **Decoration only:** every moving element added by script is `aria-hidden="true"` and removed when its animation ends; the text a screen reader gets is set at once and never moves.
  - **One-shot, short:** each plays once per trigger, at most 1.2 s; no `infinite`.
  - **Reduced motion:** the CSS sits inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, and the script checks `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` and adds nothing, so `reduce` shows the end state at once (the tip just appears, no confetti, the emoji sits still, credits don't move).
  - **Properties:** `translate`, `rotate`, `scale`, `opacity` (and `box-shadow` for the fourteenth, which is not movement). Tokens only, no raw hex.
  - **Eleventh (E9, I-095): the tip reel.** When the tip card fills and on `Another tip`, an `aria-hidden` reel over the tip text scrolls through a few tips and lands on the new one (about 900 ms, ease-out); the real text is set first.
  - **Twelfth (E9, I-099): confetti** over the result card, once, when an RSVP comes back Going (about 1 s; token colours).
  - **Thirteenth (E9, I-105): the result emoji.** Maybe 🤞 pops in and wiggles twice; Can't go 🥲 fades in, droops and rights itself (about 1 s each).
  - **Fourteenth (E10, I-102): the credit lift.** An event credit link lifts 2px with `--shadow-lift` on hover and `:focus-visible`, over `--transition`; with reduced motion the shadow still shows and nothing moves.
  - **Fifteenth (E10, I-098): the event-page entrance.** The ninth exception's `.rise`, unchanged, on the `.container` of each event-page section after the hero (§B10 E8–E11); its uses list grows by those.
- **Body map (B0, I-073, §B12): no motion exception.** Zoom and pan are instant (no animated `viewBox`), the details sheet opens without a transition, and the page has no `.rise`. It still takes part in the seventh exception's page cross-fade like every Base page.
- **Focus:** `:focus-visible { outline: var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: var(--focus-offset); }` on every interactive element.
- **Layout primitives:**
  - Container: max `--container` (72rem), side gutter 16px.
  - Sections use `--s-8` vertical padding on mobile and `--s-12` on desktop (11A; 10A had `--s-10` / `--s-16`, originally `--s-16` / `--s-24`). A closing section holding only the Book button is `.section--end`, `--s-8` at every width (11A). Home's hero: `--s-10` mobile, `--s-12` desktop (11A). Footer: `--s-6` mobile, `--s-8` desktop (11A).
  - **The first section on a page (9A, 10A)** has less top padding, `--s-6` on mobile and `--s-10` on desktop, so the H1 sits close under the header: `main > .section:first-child`. Every page except Home starts with a `.section`. Home's hero keeps its own padding.
  - **`html { scrollbar-gutter: stable; }` (9A).** `/book` loads short (its sections open on a click), so without a reserved gutter it had no scrollbar and the centred layout sat half a scrollbar to the right of every other page.
  - Breakpoint: `48rem` (tablet) only. Keep the layout simple.

### A4. Header and footer
- **Header** (sticky, `--green-900`, height `--header-h`):
  - Line logo on the left (`logo-line.png`: terracotta omega and cream lettering, made for dark backgrounds, verified). It links home (`/`). On Home only, a plain click turns the Ω once, counter-clockwise, instead of reloading; the wordmark stays still (step V, §B3 `Header`).
  - Nav: Services, Pricing, About (7A).
  - A **Book** button (CTA style) on the right.
  - On mobile, all four stay visible in one row, with no hamburger. If the width is too tight, the logo switches to the icon only (`icon.png`); 7B sets that breakpoint so nothing overflows at 360px.
  - **Logo sizes (9A):** full logo 240px wide at ≥ 48rem, 200px below that, 130px in the compact row (≤ 33rem); icon-only 48px. Header height stays `--header-h` (64px). The compact and icon-only breakpoints are set by measurement so the row never overflows.
  - Book is always reachable without scrolling (§9).
  - **Motion (M1, M2; §A3 seventh and eighth exceptions):** `view-transition-name: site-header`, so the header stays still while pages cross-fade; after 40px of scroll its hairline brightens and the logo scales to 0.88, with the header height unchanged.
- **Footer** (`--green-900`):
  - Email (`mailto:`), `site.serviceAreaSummary`, © year and legal name. **No phone number anywhere on the site** (Brian, Oct 6 2026).
  - **Credential block (I-035, step 12)**, first in the left column: `<Credentials compact />` (§B3). Renders only when `site.licensed`. **Never the license number** (`site.licenseNumber` stays empty and nothing outside `site.ts` reads it).
  - Right column (Brian, Nov 9, 2026): a `Client policies` link to `/client-policies` (step 14, I-037), then the © line and the brand credit. **No footer Book link** (removed Nov 9, 2026: the CTA band above the footer and the header Book button cover it).
  - **Spacing (Nov 9, 2026), both columns:** lines inside a group touch (line height only) and groups are `--s-4` apart. In the right column, `.site-footer__col :where(p + p) { margin-top: 0 }` removes the global `p + p` gap and `.site-footer__legal` takes `margin-top: var(--s-4)`; its groups are [Client policies] then [© line, brand credit].
  - **Brand credit (Brian, Nov 9, 2026)**, last in the right column, directly under the © line (touching it, one small group): `Brand design by John-Mark` from `site.brandCredit` (copy deck → Global). The name links to `site.brandCredit.url` with `target="_blank" rel="noopener"` and a visually hidden ` (opens in a new tab)`. Inherited cream on `--green-900` like every footer link (the `cream on green-900` pair in `check:contrast`); no new colour, opacity or size. `site.brandCredit` and the launch-party credit in `events.ts` hold the same name, role and URL; `tests/footer.test.ts` keeps them equal.

### A6. Wording (§7)
- `src/data/wording.ts` defines `w(key)`, which returns `[unlicensed, licensed][site.licensed]`.
- Copy never contains "massage therapist", "LMT", "licensed" or "massage therapy" directly. Those exist only as the licensed variants in `wording.ts`.
- While unlicensed, copy also avoids the bare word "massage".
- **Licensed (I-035, `licensed: true` from step 12):** every `w()` key returns its licensed variant, including `training` (names the school). Home is unchanged by licensure (Brian, Oct 29 2026): `heroLine` and `deepTissueHome` (Home's only `w()` keys) have equal variants, so the Home H1 stays the tagline and Home keeps "deep tissue work"; Services still uses `deepTissue` ("deep tissue massage" when licensed). The credential block (`credential`, `licensedIn`, `verifyLicense`; licensed-only, empty unlicensed variants) shows on About, `/book` and in the footer. The license number is never published: not in text, attributes, page source or JSON-LD.
- **No medical claims, ever:** don't promise to treat, cure, diagnose, fix or heal. Use reduce, support, restore movement, work with.
- All page copy comes from `docs/build/copy-deck.md` (written by Opus in step 4A). Before 4A, stub pages use only neutral placeholder text drawn from `site.ts`.

### B2. Contracts
The contract files in the repo are authoritative; read them directly. Summary:
- **`site.ts`** exports:
  - `ZoneKey`, `LinkKey`, `Rate`, `Zone`
  - `site` (the brief's §4 object plus `zones`, `zonePrecedence`, `office`, `serviceAreaSummary`, `areaServed`, `outOfRegionFeeNote`, `contact` (`lead`, `chat`: PocketSuite lead form and chat, 7A), `map`, `mapViewerUrl`, `deploy`, `licenseVerifyUrl`, `brandCredit` (`{ name, role, url }`, the footer credit, Nov 9, 2026, §A4) (step 12: DORA's license lookup, `https://apps2.colorado.gov/dora/licensing/lookup/licenselookup.aspx`, Brian, Oct 29 2026)). `licenseNumber` stays `''` and is read nowhere outside `site.ts` (I-035). `office.mapArea = {lat, lng}` (8A; `radiusKm` removed in 9R): where the Ω office mark sits, 2-decimal coordinates, **not the address**. `owner` (E13: `'Brian Clarke'`, the event-email signature and the credential line). No `phone` (7A). `rates` is `s60` and `s90` only (7A). `mapViewerUrl` is built from `map` (`mid`, `center`, `zoom`) with `URLSearchParams`. No `mapEmbedUrl` or `headerColor` since 7A (no iframe).
  - `indexable`
  - `ZoneKey = 'central' | 'midnorth' | 'north' | 'out'` and `LinkKey = 'office' | 'central' | 'midnorth' | 'north'` (step 13, I-040; were `home`/`shared`, and `LinkKey` had `general`). Display names `Central & Southwest`, `Mid-north`, `North`, `Outside my regular area` (`central` was `Central` in step 13; Brian renamed it Oct 29, 2026); no zone name contains "Springs" or "home". Names render only from `site.zones[key].name`; ServiceMap splits a name over 14 characters onto two lines (`Central &` / `Southwest`). `zonePrecedence = ['midnorth', 'central', 'north']`, `zoneOrder = ['central', 'midnorth', 'north', 'out']`.
  - `site.links` (step 13): `https://pocketsuite.io/book/ohm-precision-bodywork/items?keyword=<key>` for each `LinkKey` (Brian, Oct 29 2026). No `general` link and no placeholders.
  - `bookingUrl(key: LinkKey): string` (step 13) returns `site.links[key]`, nothing else. `isPlaceholder`, the `{href, placeholder}` object, the fallback to a general page and the `data-placeholder` attribute are gone. Components write `href={bookingUrl(key)}`.
  - `mailHref`, `zoneOrder`
- **`wording.ts`** exports `wording`, `WordingKey` and `w(key)`. Key `notSpa` added in 8A (Services intro). Keys `credential`, `licensedIn`, `verifyLicense` added for step 12 (licensed-only; unlicensed variants are `''`). Key `postNominals` added in E13: `['', 'LMT, CNMT']`, the letters after `site.owner` in the event-email signature; `credential` is now built from `site.owner` and the same constant, so its value is unchanged (`['', 'Brian Clarke, LMT, CNMT']`). Key `launchStateTest` added in E4 (I-077): `['', ' and passed his state test to become a licensed neuromuscular massage therapist']`, the licensure clause of the launch-party description (§B10), with the doc comment `/** Launch party description P1 (I-077): the licensure clause, after "650 hours of studies". Unlicensed: empty, so the sentence makes no licensure claim. */`.
- **`client-policies.ts`** (step 14, I-037): the Client Policies doc v1.4 (Oct 29, 2026), client-facing sections only (nothing from its "Drafting notes"), with the two I-037 changes. The text is in the copy deck → Client Policies; this file renders it as data. Imports `site` and `type Rate` from `./site.ts`; no other import (the tests import it under Node's type stripping, so no `enum`, `namespace` or parameter properties). Exports:
  ```ts
  export type Run = string | { text: string; href: string };      // an inline link inside running text
  export type Rich = string | Run[];
  export type Block =
    | { type: 'paragraph'; text: Rich }
    | { type: 'bullets'; items: { lead?: string; text: Rich }[] }  // lead renders bold, then a space, then text
    | { type: 'table'; caption: string; head: string[]; rows: string[][] }  // rows[i][0] is the row header
    | { type: 'notice'; columns: [{ head: string; text: string }, { head: string; text: string }] };
  export interface PolicySection { id: string; title: string; blocks: Block[] }
  export interface ClientPolicies { version: string; date: string; displayDate: string; intro: string; sections: PolicySection[] }

  export const terms: { surchargePercent: 3; noticeHours: 24; lateCancelPercent: 50; checkInMinutes: 15;
                        graceMinutes: 15; groupMax: 4; reportDays: 7 };            // as const
  export const packages: { sessions: 5; expiryMonths: 12;
                           prices: { s60: { office: 375; mobile: 475 }; s90: { office: 500; mobile: 600 } } };  // as const
  export function lateCancelFee(rate: Rate): number;                    // rate.price * terms.lateCancelPercent / 100 → 45, 60
  export function packageSavings(key: 's60' | 's90', place: 'office' | 'mobile'): number;
      // office: sessions × rate − price; mobile: sessions × (rate + site.travelFee.amount) − price → 75/100, 100/125
  export const coloradoNotice: string;   // the statutory notice, verbatim (copy deck → Client Policies)
  export const surchargeLine: string;    // `${site.name} adds a ${terms.surchargePercent}% surcharge to credit card payments. No surcharge on cash, Zelle, or debit cards.`
  export const acceptedPayments: string; // (step 15 prep, I-041) Booking and payment bullet 3, verbatim: 'I accept cash, Zelle, and credit or debit cards through PocketSuite (Tap to Pay in person, or the booking link).'
  export const zelleDetails: string;     // (step 15 prep) bullet 4, verbatim: "Ask me for Zelle details. I don't accept Venmo, PayPal or other payment apps."
  export const paymentMethodsLine: string; // (step 15 prep) `${acceptedPayments} ${zelleDetails}`, the PaymentNotice methods line
  export const policiesPdfPath = '/ohm-client-policies.pdf';           // pass through href()
  export const clientPolicies: ClientPolicies;  // version '1.4', date '2026-10-29', displayDate 'Oct 29, 2026'
  ```
  - **Sections, in order** (`id` · `title`): `booking` · Booking and payment; `cancelling` · Cancelling and rescheduling; `late-arrival` · Late arrival and no-shows; `illness` · Illness and skin conditions; `mobile-visits` · Mobile visits and travel; `packages` · Packages; `not-right` · If a session wasn't right; `tips` · Tips; `communication` · Communication; `conduct` · Conduct and safety. Ids are stable: shared links use them.
  - **Derived, never typed:** rates, minutes and the travel fee from `site.rates` / `site.travelFee.amount`; the domain is `new URL(site.deploy.customDomain).host`; the email is `site.email` (a `Run` linking `mailHref`); "contact form" and "chat" are `Run`s linking `site.contact.lead` / `site.contact.chat`; late-cancel fees, package savings, the 75/105-minute totals (`minutes + terms.checkInMinutes`) and the 5 × sessions from the functions and constants above. Package prices and the 12-month expiry live only here (they are policy, not site facts). The domain is plain text, not a link (it redirects to PocketSuite until launch).
  - **Never in this file:** a phone number, a Zelle address or handle, `[Zelle address]` or any other bracketed placeholder, drafting notes.
  - **Payment text has one source** (step 15 prep, I-041): the `booking` section's bullets 3 and 4 are `{ text: acceptedPayments }` and `{ text: zelleDetails }`, so the policies page, the PDF check and `PaymentNotice` read the same strings. No payment method is added or named anywhere else (no ACH or bank transfer, no Zelle address or handle; Venmo and PayPal only as not accepted).
- **The PDF follows this file** (I-043): the test reads the committed PDF's text and fails while any sentence here, or a figure it reads from `site.ts`, is missing from it (§B9).
- **`geo.ts`** exports `LngLat`, `Ring`, `ZoneFeature`, `ZoneCollection`, `BBox`, `pointInRing`, `pointInPolygon`, `bboxOf(fc, zone?)` (7A) and `zoneFor(lat, lng, fc)`.
- **`tokens.css`** adds `--zone-central`, `--zone-midnorth`, `--zone-north` (7A; renamed from `--zone-home`/`--zone-shared` in step 13), and `--zone-{central|midnorth|north}-tint` (8A: `color-mix` of the zone colour at 40% into `--bg-light`). **The tints are what the eye sees:** the map fills them opaque, and the area buttons use them as their background. `--zone-out-tint` (9A: ink 15% into `--bg-light`) is the "outside" area's colour, shown on the map only while hovered or chosen, and on the chosen out button. (`--zone-muted` was deleted in 9R.)
- **`url.ts`:**
  ```ts
  export function href(path: string): string
  ```
  - Joins `import.meta.env.BASE_URL` and `path`, with no double slashes.
  - With base `/` (I-018): `href('/')` → `/`. `href('/book')` → `/book`. Under any other base the base is prefixed (base `/x` gives `/x/book`).
  - External URLs (`http…`, `tel:`, `sms:`, `mailto:`) pass through unchanged.

  **Every internal link and `fetch` must use `href`.**

### B3. Component props

| Component | Props | Renders |
|---|---|---|
| `Base` | `title: string; description: string; ogImage?: ImageMetadata; ogAlt?: string; jsonLd?: Record<string, unknown>; noindex?: boolean; bare?: boolean; analytics?: boolean = true` (9A: `bare` drops the skip link, Header and Footer; used only by `/hello`, §B8. A1, §B11: `analytics={false}` drops the Umami tag, the `analytics-rules` meta and the click script; `/body-map` is dropped by path whatever it passes; `bare` pages get the tag but not the click script). **`ogImage` (E1; listed here before, never built):** when set, the OG/Twitter image is a `fit: 'cover'` JPEG crop of it at 1.905:1, never upscaled: `w = min(1200, src.width)`, `h = round(w / 1.905)`; if `h > src.height` then `h = src.height`, `w = round(h * 1.905)`. `og:image:width`/`height` carry the real `w`/`h`; `og:image:alt` is `ogAlt` when given. ### B4. Booking router (`/book`)

**Static markup (works with JS off):**
```html
<h1>Book a session</h1>
<fieldset id="where" hidden>                     <!-- JS un-hides -->
  <legend>Where do you want your session?</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="where" value="office"> At my office</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="where" value="mobile"> At your place</label>
</fieldset>
<section id="office" aria-labelledby="office-h"> <OfficeCard/> <ServiceMap focus="office" id="office-map"/> </section>  <!-- map 8A -->
<section id="mobile" aria-labelledby="mobile-h" data-maps-key={key}>
  <h2 id="mobile-h">Where are you located?</h2>  <!-- 7A order: areas, then address -->
  <ZonePicker/>                                  <!-- no heading here -->
  <div id="address-slot"></div>                 <!-- 3B combobox; label "Not sure? Enter your address:" (9A) -->
  <div id="zone-result" aria-live="polite"></div>
  <ServiceMap/>
  <p>Near a boundary or can't find your address? <a href={site.contact.chat}>Chat with me</a> or <a href={mailHref}>send me an email</a>. Boundaries are approximate.</p>  <!-- 9A -->
</section>
<template data-zone="central"><ZoneCard zone="central" headingLevel={3}/></template>  … one per ZoneKey (via='pick')
<template data-zone="out" data-via="address"><ZoneCard zone="out" via="address" headingLevel={3}/></template>
<script> import '../../scripts/book.ts' </script>
```
- With JS off, both sections show in order (office first) and every zone link works.
- `key = import.meta.env.PUBLIC_GOOGLE_MAPS_KEY ?? ''`.

**`/book/[zone]`:** `getStaticPaths` → `central`, `midnorth`, `north`, `out`, `office` (step 13: `/book/home` and `/book/shared` are gone, with no redirect pages; the site is not launched, so nothing outside links to them).
- The page has an H1 "Book a session" and the card for that zone (`OfficeCard` for `office`), at heading level 2. The `out` card uses `via='pick'`.
- Under the card: `<ServiceMap focus={zone} />`, so the static page shows the zone zoomed with the others greyed. On the office page it's `<ServiceMap focus="office" />` (8A).
- It also has `ZonePicker current=… heading="Not sure? Pick your area."` and links "Back to booking options" → `/book` and "At my office" → `/book/office` (the latter omitted on the office page).
- One client script, `terrain.ts` (I-054), from `ServiceMap`: it only loads the terrain shading. Nothing else on the page uses JS; with JS off the map shows without terrain.

**`book.ts` state machine (7A):**
```
init: un-hide #where; hide #office and #mobile; no radio checked.
  Intercept clicks on #mobile .zone-picker links and on map zones → select(zone, 'pick').
  Un-hide .map-hint; add class "is-interactive" to the map svg.
choose(office) → show #office, hide #mobile.
choose(mobile) → show #mobile, hide #office; if first time and data-maps-key non-empty → loadPlaces().
loadPlaces: idle → loading → ready | unavailable   (unchanged from 3B; Places only)
  ready: render combobox in #address-slot.
  unavailable: empty #address-slot. The map and picker never depend on Google. No console output.
select(zone, via, loc?):
  clone <template data-zone=zone data-via=via> if it exists, else <template data-zone=zone>,
    into #zone-result, then focus the cloned heading;
  aria-current="true" on the picker link for zone (remove it from the others);
  map: focusZone(zone, loc) and setPin(loc) (no loc → hide the pin).
  via 'pick' also clears the address input.
  .map-reset visible iff zone is central|midnorth|north (8A).
address selection → select(zoneFor(...), 'address', {lat, lng}).
deselect() (8A): empty #zone-result; remove aria-current from every picker link; setPin(null);
  clear the address input; map back to the full view, no is-focused/is-muted, --map-scale 1;
  hide .map-reset. Focus stays where it is, except: if focus was inside #zone-result or on
  .map-reset, move it to the first picker link.
  Triggers: click a picker link that already has aria-current; click the map area that has
  is-focused; click .map-reset.
hot(zone | null) (8A): pointerenter/focusin on a zone picker link → is-hot on the map area
  (fill + outline paths) of that zone; pointerenter on a map area → is-hot on its picker link;
  pointerleave/focusout → hot(null). Never for 'out'. Purely visual; no announcements.
9A changes:
  'out' is a full peer: the map has an out area (path.zone--out, everything outside the zones).
    Clicking it selects/deselects 'out'; hot() covers 'out'; .map-reset shows for any chosen zone.
  focusZone(out): full view (widened for a pin), out area is-focused, the three zones is-muted.
  is-muted = the zone keeps its tint, dimmed (fill-opacity 0.35), no longer grey.
  office link: a plain left click on .map-office → preventDefault(); goOffice():
    check the office radio, choose(office), scroll #office into view, focus #office-h.
    Without JS the badge is a link to /book/office.
```
- **Zone-picker links with JS on (7A):** on `/book` they're intercepted, so the map stays on the page. Without JS they navigate to `/book/<zone>`, which shows the same map zoomed to that zone.
- **Map (7A): our own SVG, no map service.** Brian chose this over a Maps JS map (Dynamic Maps billing, a heavier page, an iframe fallback). Rollback path if he doesn't like it: the Maps JS design is kept in `steps/7A-review-contracts.md` → "Alternative: Maps JS map".
  - **Data:** `src/data/zones.geojson` (zones) and `src/data/osm.geojson` (roads + places, `npm run osm`, committed). Nothing is fetched at runtime.
  - **Projection (`mapview.ts`):** equirectangular scaled by `cos(lat0)`. At this size it's indistinguishable from Web Mercator. `x = (lng − west) · cos(lat0) · k`, `y = (north − lat) · k`, with the full view 1000 units wide. The **full view** is `bboxOf(zones)` padded 6% and widened to a **4:5** (w:h) box around its centre. That gives context east and west (Falcon, Manitou) and stops it being a tall strip. `viewFor(bbox)` returns a 4:5 box in SVG units that contains `bbox` padded 10%. The client imports the same module, so the build and the pin use the same maths.
  - **Layers, bottom to top:** panel background `--bg-light`; zone fills (9A: the out area first); terrain (9A); minor roads (9A); roads; zone outlines; road labels; place labels; zone labels; office badge (9A); pin. The `<svg>` is `role="img"`, named by a `hidden` `<span>` before it (`Service area map`; not an svg `<title>`, which shows as a hover tooltip over the whole map; Oct 6, after 11R) and a `<desc>` naming the three zones and the roads shown. Interactive paths are a pointer-only extra; the buttons are the keyboard path.
  - **Styling (tokens only, classes not inline colours):** zones `fill: var(--zone-{key}-tint)`, opaque (8A; was `--zone-{key}` at 0.35), stroke `var(--zone-{key})`, 2px; `is-hot` stroke 4px. Roads `--ink` at 0.45: I-25 2.5px, others 1.5px. All strokes `vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke`. Labels: `--ink`, DM Sans, with a `--bg-light` halo (`paint-order: stroke`). Zone labels 700 weight. Road labels short names (I-25, US 24, Hwy 83, Academy, Woodmen, Powers, Garden of the Gods, Austin Bluffs, Templeton Gap, Baptist). Place labels italic at 0.7 opacity. **9A:** minor roads `--ink` at 0.22, 1px, no labels. Out area `--zone-out-tint`, `fill-opacity` 0 (still clickable), 0.6 when `is-hot`, 1 when `is-focused`; no outline. Muted zones keep their tint at `fill-opacity: 0.35`.
  - **Label placement (build time):** a zone label sits at its polygon's pole of inaccessibility (a grid search for the interior point farthest from an edge; no dependency). A road label sits at a vertex near the middle of the road's longest piece inside the full view. `ServiceMap` keeps a small `labelNudge` table (zone/road → `[dx, dy]` in SVG units) for hand fixes.
  - **Zoom:** JS swaps the `viewBox`, with no animation (§A3 restraint). `focusZone(central|midnorth|north)` → `viewFor(bboxOf(zones, zone))`, adds `is-focused` to that zone and `is-muted` to the others (9A: own tint at 0.35, was `--zone-muted` at 0.06; outline opacity 0.25). `focusZone(out)` → the full view, extended to include the pin if it's outside; 9A: the out area `is-focused`, the three zones `is-muted`. To keep text and the pin the same on-screen size, JS sets `--map-scale` (full width ÷ current width) on the svg. Labels and the pin use `font-size: calc(… / var(--map-scale))` and `transform: scale(calc(1 / var(--map-scale)))`.
  - **Pin:** a `<g class="map-pin" hidden>` in the SVG (teardrop path, `--accent` fill, `--bg-light` outline). `setPin({lat,lng})` projects with `mapview.ts` and sets its translate. `null` hides it.
  - **Office map (8A, revised 9A, 10A):** `ServiceMap focus="office"`. **10A:** a `Show mobile service areas` link-button over its top-right corner (the same dark style as `Show all areas`): `<a class="map-areas" href="/book#mobile">` (base-aware). On `/book`, book.ts turns a plain click into `goMobile()` ("At your place", full map, scroll and focus its heading); `/book#mobile` on load does the same, so the link from `/book/office` lands there. Without JS, `/book` shows both sections and the hash scrolls. It has no zone layers. **View (9A):** the Central zoom, `frame.viewFor(bboxOf(zones, 'central'))`, widened with `frame.include(…, ox, oy, 120)` so the office is never at an edge (8A's 12 km `viewAround` was too close for the detail the map has; `viewAround` stays in `mapview.ts`, unused). `--map-scale` = full width ÷ view width. Terrain, minor roads, roads and places as usual, clipped to the view. The office mark at the projected `site.office.mapArea` point, not a link, labelled `Ohm Office` like every other map (9C; was `My office is in this area`). No circle (9A), no teardrop. No JS beyond that link and the terrain loader (`terrain.ts`, I-054), no zones, no reset. Shown in `#office` on `/book` and on `/book/office`. `<title>`/`<desc>` from the copy deck.
  - **Office mark (9A, revised after 9B by Brian):** just the Ω, no disc. It's an inline nested `<svg>` of the traced path `omega.json` `dMap` (a coarser simplification for map size), about 105 map units wide at scale 1 (10A; ~34px on a phone), `--accent` fill with a 3px `--bg-light` halo (`paint-order: stroke`), and the label **`Ohm Office`** under it on every map view (zone-label style). Counter-scaled with `--map-scale`, like the pin, so it's the same size at every zoom. Other labels move out of its way (nudges), never the mark. *(9B shipped a disc badge first: the `icon.png` image on a cream disc with a terracotta ring. 9C replaces it.)* It sits on `site.office.mapArea` (2 decimals, ~1 km: approximate on purpose). On zone-mode maps it's wrapped in `<a class="map-office" href="/book/office" tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true">` with `<title>My office</title>`: a pointer-only extra, like the map areas; the keyboard path is the "At my office" radio. On `/book`, book.ts turns the click into `goOffice()`.
  - **Hover dimming (10A):** on the `/book` mobile map, hovering an area (map or button, as the linked hover) or the office mark dims everything else: the other region fills to `fill-opacity: 0.35` and the office mark to `opacity: 0.5`; the hovered area shows its full tint even if it's muted. Hovering `out` dims the three regions and the mark. Leaving restores the current state. Classes, set by `hot()`: `is-dim` on the dimmed elements.
  - **Map buttons (10A):** `Show all areas` and `Show mobile service areas` are dark (`--bg-dark` fill, `--text-on-dark` text, soft shadow) so they read on the light map.
  - **Terrain (9A):** `<image class="terrain">` of `src/assets/terrain.webp` stretched over the projected `terrain.json` bbox with `preserveAspectRatio="none"`. The image is sampled on a regular lng/lat grid, and `project` is linear in lng and lat, so it lines up exactly and is independent of the zones. It's black with alpha (shadow only), so on flat ground the zone tints are exact. CSS `opacity` (~0.6, tuned in 9B) sets the strength. `pointer-events: none`. **Deferred (I-054, decision I-055 option A; Brian, Nov 5 2026):** the `<image>` carries `data-href={terrainImg.src}`, not `href`, and `ServiceMap` has `<script> import '../scripts/terrain.ts'; </script>` (Astro bundles it as one module script per page, once even when the page has two maps). `src/scripts/terrain.ts` (client script 4) waits for the window `load` event (or starts at once if `document.readyState === 'complete'`), then an `IntersectionObserver` watches each map `<svg>` holding an `image.terrain[data-href]`; when one intersects it sets `href` from `data-href` and unobserves it. So on `/book` the ~192 KB terrain is fetched only once a visitor picks a place and a map shows; on `/book/{central,midnorth,north,office,out}` after load. No storage, no console, no network beyond the image. With JS off the maps show without terrain: it is decoration only, and the zone links and booking still work. Why: `fetchpriority="low"` has no effect on an SVG `<image>` (Chrome keeps it Medium); Lighthouse 13.5 mobile on `astro preview`: `/book` 96 → 100 (LCP 2.71 → 1.66 s), `/book/central` 97 → 100 (2.56 → 1.58 s), `/book/office` 98 → 100 (2.41 → 1.43 s). Rejected: a no-JS lazy `<img>` in `<foreignObject>` (in WebKit the shading stopped short of the map's left edge). Test: `tests/terrain-defer.test.ts`.
  - **Static maps clip (9A):** a map with a `focus` never zooms, so its road lines are clipped to its view plus 5%. Only the `/book` mobile map carries every road.
  - **Size:** full width of the container, `max-width: 34rem`, aspect 4:5, `--radius`, 1px `--line-dark` border. Inline SVG budgets (9A): the `/book` mobile map ≤ 70 KB, each static map ≤ 40 KB. Tune minor-road simplification in `npm run osm` to fit.
- **Privacy (7A):** the pin's coordinates live only in memory and in an SVG `transform`. Nothing is requested to draw them.
- **Cost (7A):** the map costs nothing. Google is used only for Places autocomplete (unchanged). The README's `Map loads per day` cap stays as a guard.
- **Keyboard:** native radios and links. The combobox follows the ARIA 1.2 combobox pattern (step 3B).
- **Privacy:** the address input value is never written to storage, the URL, the console, or any request other than Google's.
- **Google specifics:** pinned in step 3A. The spec of record is `steps/3B-zones-autocomplete.md` § "Google spec".
  - Places API (New) via Maps JS. Loaded with the **direct script tag** (`loading=async` + `callback`), not the inline bootstrap, which contains a `console.warn`. Then `google.maps.importLibrary('places')`.
  - Autocomplete: `AutocompleteSuggestion.fetchAutocompleteSuggestions` with an `AutocompleteSessionToken`, `includedRegionCodes: ['us']`, a location bias toward Colorado Springs, a minimum of 3 characters and a 300ms debounce.
  - On selection: `toPlace().fetchFields({ fields: ['location', 'formattedAddress'] })`.
  - Unavailable when any of these happens: the import rejects, a 6s timeout, `gm_authFailure`, or an error is thrown. Any Places call that rejects also counts. A bad key surfaces only this way, on the first query (3R).

### B5. Scripts and CI

**`npm run check:wording`** (`scripts/check-wording.mjs`, no dependencies):
- Reads `site.licensed` by dynamically importing `../src/data/site.ts` (Node ≥22.18/24 strips types natively).
- Walks `dist/**/*.html`. For each file it:
  - removes `<script>…</script>` and `<style>…</style>` blocks
  - collects the values of `alt`, `title`, `aria-label`, `placeholder`, and `<meta content>`
  - strips the remaining tags
  - decodes `&amp; &#39; &quot; &lt; &gt; &nbsp;`
- **Flags (step 12):** `--dist <dir>` (default `dist`) and `--licensed true|false` (default `site.licensed`), so its test can run both states on synthetic trees.
- **When `licensed === false`:** it fails (exit 1) on `/\bmassage\s+therap(?:ist|y)\b|\bLMT\b|\blicensed\b/i`. It prints the file path and roughly 60 characters of context for each hit.
- **When `licensed === true` (step 12):** every page except `hello.html` and `hello/index.html` must contain `wording.credential[1]` and `wording.licensedIn[1]` in its visible text and `href="{site.licenseVerifyUrl}"` in its raw HTML; `about.html` and `book.html` must exist and contain `wording.credential[1]` at least twice in their visible text (their own block plus the footer). Each miss fails (exit 1) with the file and the missing piece.
- **Always (step 12):** fail if any JSON-LD block (`<script type="application/ld+json">…</script>`) contains `"hasCredential"` or `"identifier"`; fail if the visible text matches `/\blicen[cs]e\s*(?:no\b\.?|number\b|#)/i`; fail if `site.licenseNumber` is non-empty (message `licenseNumber must stay empty (I-035)`), and then also name every file whose raw HTML contains it.
- **Always (step 13, I-040):** fail (exit 1) when the visible text (including the collected attribute and `<meta content>` values) matches `/\bhome[\s-]+(?:visits?|office|mobile)\b/i`: "home visit(s)", "home office", "Home mobile", any case, a space or hyphen between the words. Print the file and ~60 characters of context for each hit, like the licensed-term hits. The rule (BRIEF §7): a session at the client's place is a "mobile visit", at Brian's space an "office session". "home page" and the logo's `aria-label` "Ohm Precision Bodywork, home" stay allowed.
- **Always:** it warns, without failing, on `/\b(?:treat|cure|diagnos|fix|heal)\w*/i`. The allowlist covers phrases containing `substitute for medical diagnosis`. It prints the hits for review.
- It exits 2 with a clear message if `dist/` is missing.

**`npm run zones`** (`scripts/kml-to-geojson.mjs`, no dependencies):
- **Arguments:** `[kmlPath = 'brief/Ohm Service Map.kml'] [--out src/data/zones.geojson]`.
- **Parsing (6A):** placemarks without a `<Polygon>` (pins, lines) are skipped and only counted. For each polygon placemark it reads `<name>`, decodes CDATA and `&amp;`, trims and collapses whitespace, and matches it **exactly** against `site.zones[key].name` for `central`, `midnorth` and `north` (imported from `src/data/site.ts`). Since step 13 (I-040) those names are `Mid-north` and `North`, and since Oct 29, 2026 `Central & Southwest` (step 13 had `Central`). The polygons in Brian's local KML must carry exactly these names; in KML the `&` is written `&amp;` or inside CDATA (were `Central & Southwest Springs`, `Mid-north Springs`, `North Springs`). There is no `out` polygon: a point in no polygon is `out`. An unknown polygon name exits 1 and lists both the names found and the names expected.
- **Geometry:** it collects every `<Polygon>`. The `<outerBoundaryIs>` ring comes first, then the `<innerBoundaryIs>` rings. It parses `lng,lat[,alt]` triples, drops the altitude, and rounds to 6 decimal places. Several polygons on one placemark become a `MultiPolygon`.
- **Output:** only `{type, properties:{zone}, geometry}`. It ignores and **never emits** `<description>`, `<ExtendedData>`, styles, Points and LineStrings, and logs a count of what it skipped.
- It fails if a zone key is missing or appears twice.
- It writes 2-space JSON with one feature per zone, in the order central, midnorth, north.

**`npm run osm`** (`scripts/fetch-osm.mjs`, no dependencies, run by hand, never in CI) (7A):
- Queries the Overpass API (`https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter`, with a `User-Agent` naming the site; retry once after 30s on a non-JSON "too busy" reply) for the box `38.63,-105.09,39.17,-104.54` (S,W,N,E). That's the full view (lng −104.996…−104.635, lat 38.724…39.076) plus ~25% each side, so a widened `out` view still has roads (7B unblock):
  - ways with `highway` ~ `motorway|trunk|primary|secondary|tertiary` (no `_link`) whose `name` matches `^(North |South |East |West )?(Academy Boulevard|Woodmen Road|Powers Boulevard|Garden of the Gods Road|Austin Bluffs Parkway|Baptist Road|Templeton Gap Road)$`
  - `motorway|trunk` ways with `ref` containing `I 25` or `US 24`, and any `highway` way with `ref` `CO 83`
  - `place` ~ `city|town|village|hamlet` nodes named `Manitou Springs|Monument|Falcon|Fountain|Black Forest|Security|Widefield|Colorado Springs`
- OSM has no `Security-Widefield` node. The output's `Security-Widefield` place is the mean of the `Security` and `Widefield` nodes (`COMBINED` in the script), so there are still 7 places.
- Groups the ways into one road per short name (the list in §B4 "Styling"), **joins ways that share an endpoint into chains**, clips the chains to the box, and simplifies each piece (Douglas–Peucker, ~0.0004°). It rounds coordinates to 5 decimals. Without the join, OSM's short ways leave ~3,200 vertices in ~1,500 two-point lines; with it, ~570 vertices (Oct 6 run).
- `ServiceMap` draws everything in `osm.geojson` with no second clip. Features outside the current `viewBox` are simply off-canvas (Falcon, Fountain and Monument sit just outside the full view and appear when a pin widens it).
- Writes `src/data/osm.geojson`: road features `{ kind: 'road', name: <short>, major: boolean }` as `MultiLineString`, and place features `{ kind: 'place', name }` as `Point`. It writes no other OSM tags and no IDs.
- Prints feature and vertex counts. Exits 1 if any expected road or place is missing.
- **Licence:** OSM data is ODbL. The map shows the credit line, and the README notes that `osm.geojson` is ODbL-licensed.
- **Minor roads (9A):** the query also takes every `primary|secondary` way in the box. Ways that aren't one of the named roads go into one pool: joined, clipped, simplified (`SIMPLIFY_MINOR_DEG` 0.0006, up to 0.001 for the size budget), pieces under `MIN_MINOR_KM` (1, up to 2) dropped. Output: one feature `{ kind: 'minor' }` (no name), written before the named roads.

**`npm run terrain`** (`scripts/make-terrain.mjs`, 9A; `sharp` like `make-icons.mjs`; run by hand, never in CI):
- Source: AWS Terrain Tiles, Terrarium PNG, `https://s3.amazonaws.com/elevation-tiles-prod/terrarium/12/{x}/{y}.png` (checked Oct 6 2026). `elevation_m = R × 256 + G + B / 256 − 32768`. US data is USGS 3DEP, public domain; credit `3DEP data courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey` (README) and `Terrain: USGS 3DEP` (map credit line).
- Tiles cached in `.cache/terrain/` (gitignored); a rerun downloads nothing.
- Box = the OSM box. Output grid regular in lng/lat, 1024 px wide, height for square ground pixels. Bilinear elevation sampling, Horn hillshade (azimuth 315°, altitude 45°), shadow alpha `(1 − shade / sin 45°)^0.8`, RGB black. WebP with alpha, < 200 KB, to `src/assets/terrain.webp`; `{bbox, width, height}` to `src/data/terrain.json`.

**`npm run omega`** (`scripts/trace-omega.mjs`, 9A; `sharp`, no other dependency): alpha ≥ 128 mask of `src/assets/icon.png`, largest component, outer contour by marching squares, Douglas–Peucker at 1.5px, integer coordinates, viewBox = bbox + 2%. Writes `src/data/omega.json`. Temporary: JohnMark's SVG replaces it (TODO(Brian)). **10A:** the closed contour (for `d` and `dMap` alike) starts at the right foot's inner corner, the vertex where the hand cut-out meets the baseline on the right (the lowest-right vertex of the cut-out's right edge), and runs clockwise on screen (positive shoelace area with y down). `omega.test.ts` pins both.

**`npm run check:dist`** (`scripts/check-dist.mjs`, 9A, no dependencies; runs in CI after `check:wording`): fails if `dist/hello.html` lacks `noindex` (whatever `indexable` is), has a canonical to another page, or has a `<script src>` other than the Umami tag (A1, §B11) or more than one inline script besides JSON-LD (10A: the click-pause script is allowed); if `sitemap.xml` mentions `hello`; if `robots.txt` disallows `/hello` by name; if any other page links to `hello`; or if `index.html` carries splash markup. **A1 (§B11):** fails if any page built from Base (not `body-map`, not redirect stubs) lacks exactly one Umami tag with `data-website-id` and `data-domains` equal to the production hostname, or if `body-map.html` / `body-map/index.html` carries any analytics marker (passes when neither exists). `--dist <dir>` for its test.

**Client policies PDF** (I-043): no script. `npm run policies:pdf` and `scripts/make-policies-pdf.mjs` (step 14, Playwright printing the page) are retired, with the hash file `src/data/client-policies.pdf.json`. Brian builds the branded PDF in his doc kit from the policy text and saves it over `public/ohm-client-policies.pdf`; the text check in §B9 keeps it honest. Playwright stays for `tools/shots.mjs`. Run `npm run build` after replacing the PDF so `dist/` carries it (CI builds anyway).

**`npm test`:** `node --test "tests/**/*.test.ts"`, using Node's built-in runner and `node:assert/strict`. Tests import from `../src/lib/geo.ts` and read `../src/data/zones.geojson` via `fs`.

**`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`:**
```yaml
on: { push: { branches: [main] }, workflow_dispatch: {} }
permissions: { contents: read, pages: write, id-token: write }
concurrency: { group: pages, cancel-in-progress: false }
jobs:
  build:   runs-on ubuntu-latest
    steps: actions/checkout@v7 · actions/setup-node@v7 (node-version: 24, cache: npm) · npm ci · npm test ·
           npm run build (env PUBLIC_GOOGLE_MAPS_KEY: ${{ vars.PUBLIC_GOOGLE_MAPS_KEY }}) ·
           npm run check:wording · npm run check:dist (9A) · actions/configure-pages@v6 · actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5 (path: dist)
  deploy:  needs: build; environment: { name: github-pages, url: ${{ steps.d.outputs.page_url }} }
    steps: actions/deploy-pages@v5 (id: d)
```
These action versions were checked on Oct 5 2026.

### B7. SEO (step 5A)
- **Per-page meta:** `title` and `description` come from the copy deck. The title format is `{Page} · Ohm Precision Bodywork`; the home page uses `Ohm Precision Bodywork · Neuromuscular therapy in Colorado Springs`.
- **`robots.txt.ts`:** when `indexable` is false, it emits `User-agent: *\nDisallow: /`. When true, `Allow: /` plus a `Sitemap:` line.
- **`sitemap.xml.ts`:** lists `/`, `/services`, `/pricing`, `/about`, `/book` and `/client-policies` (step 14) with absolute URLs from `Astro.site` and the base, plus `/events/<slug>` (E8, I-092; was `/<slug>`) for each event with `index: true` (E1, §B10; the launch party has `index: false`, so it is not listed; the `/<slug>` redirect pages are never listed). Never `/hello` (9A, §B8), never `/events/*.ics` or `.json`, never `/body-map` (B0, §B12; `robots.txt` doesn't name it either, so crawlers can still read its `noindex`).
- **JSON-LD:** a `HealthAndBeautyBusiness` (a `LocalBusiness` subtype). Confirmed in 5R: `MedicalBusiness` subtypes would frame the work as medical, which §7 rules out while unlicensed.
  - Fields: `name`, `url`, `email` (no `telephone`, 7A), `areaServed` (City list from `site.areaServed`), `priceRange: "$90–$120"` (derived from rates, not hardcoded), and `image` (the OG image).
  - **No street address.**
  - **No licensure fields, ever (I-035; resolves I-027):** no `hasCredential`, no `identifier`, no license number. `check:wording` fails on them.
- **OG image:** a 1200×630 `getImage` crop of the landscape photo.

### B8. `/hello` entrance page (9A, step 9C)
**Decision (Brian, Oct 6, 2026):** the splash is its own page, not an overlay on Home. A full-screen splash on arrival from search trips Google's intrusive-interstitial signal and gets between search visitors and prices and booking. `/hello` is the deliberate entrance for people who come from a business card, QR code, social bio or referral. **Printed materials, QR codes and social bios link to `/hello`; search, Maps and the Google Business Profile link to `/`.** Home has no overlay.
The spec of record is `steps/9C-hello.md`; this is the summary.
- **Page:** `src/pages/hello.astro`, `Base noindex bare` (no skip link, header or footer). The whole page is one `<a class="hello" href="/">` (base-aware) holding the body graphic, a `.hello-mark` wrapper with an inline SVG Ω from `src/data/omega.json` (fill, hover glow, light and pulse paths) and the `(Enter)` cue, and the line `Take the path of least resistance`. **Art (Brian, Nov 1 2026):** `src/assets/graphic-green-hd.png` (the full drawing's original pixels, the old crop re-cut and upscaled 3.2x, 2000px wide), `widths={[800, 1200, 1600, 2000]}`, `sizes="100vh"`: the art is as tall as the screen and about as wide as it is tall, so `100vw` picked files far too small on phones. It sits at `right: -8%`; on desktop (≥ 48rem) at `right: 2%`, so the back sits partly behind the Ω, with the left edge faded into the green (`mask-image`, as on the Home hero). **Cue (Brian, Nov 1 2026):** `<span class="hello-cue" aria-hidden="true">(Enter)</span>` inside `.hello-mark`, after the svg, absolutely placed low in the Ω's palm above the wrist (`bottom: 14%`, centred); capitals by CSS, the line's size (`--line-fs`) and its 75% cream. It glows (`text-shadow`) on `:focus-visible`, `.is-entering` and, on fine pointers, page hover. The accessible name is a visually hidden "Enter Ohm Precision Bodywork." plus the line (the cue is `aria-hidden`). Entering is plain navigation; Back returns to `/hello`.
- **Analytics (A1, I-114; §B11):** `/hello` is tracked (it is the card, QR and social entrance). The no-`<script src>` rule is relaxed for exactly one external script, the Umami tag; no other `src` script, and Base's click script is not loaded here. The one-inline-script limit below stays. `check:dist` enforces both.
- **JavaScript (10A):** one inline script (`is:inline`, ~10 lines), only for the click pause: a plain click or Enter adds `.is-entering` (the glow) and navigates after 500ms. Modified clicks pass through; reduced motion navigates at once; `pageshow` (`persisted`) clears the class after Back. Without JS the link navigates at once. Everything else is CSS. (9C shipped with no JS at all; Brian accepted the script in 10A.)
- **Motion (10A):** the light starts at the right foot's inner corner (where the hand meets the baseline) and runs clockwise: up the thumb side, across the fingers, down the palm, along the left foot, over the arch, down the right leg and back. One lap takes 3s (11A; was 4.5s) from 0.4s, and it runs once (Brian, Nov 1 2026; it used to repeat every 11s): then the breath and the cue take over. The light and glow have no `non-scaling-stroke`: with it, browsers lay dashes out in screen space while `pathLength` normalises in viewBox space, so the lap ran 1/scale too fast (2.5× on phones). Their widths are viewBox units (light 5, glow 8). The line fades in as the lap ends (`ohm-reveal`, 1s from 3.4s) and stays. **One breath clock (Brian, Nov 1 2026):** `.hello` sets `--breathe-delay: 1.5s` (was a fixed 4.4s on each element), so the breath starts during the lap and there is never a dead moment; the line, `.hello-mark` and the glow pulse all start on it. **Line breathing (F2, I-039; Brian, Oct 29 2026):** `.hello-line` breathes with keyframe `ohm-breathe`: `transform: scale(1)` to `scale(1.05)` and back, 6s per cycle (3s in, 3s out), `ease-in-out`, `infinite`, `animation-delay: var(--breathe-delay)`, `transform-origin: center`. CSS only: no JS added, `check:dist` unchanged. **Ω breathing (step V trial, Oct 30 2026; wrapper Nov 1 2026, Brian):** the `.hello-mark` wrapper (the Ω svg and the `(Enter)` cue, as one element) breathes with the line: the same `ohm-breathe` keyframes, `6s ease-in-out var(--breathe-delay) infinite`, `transform` on the wrapper only (nothing inside it). Same duration and delay as `.hello-line`, so the two stay in step: the line's tracking is sized to span the Ω's ink width, so both scale together (each about its own centre). **Glow pulse (Brian, Nov 1 2026):** a second glow path, `.omega-pulse`, runs `ohm-hello-glow` (opacity 0 to 0.6 and back) `6s ease-in-out var(--breathe-delay) infinite`, so the Ω lights up at the top of each inhale and touch screens get the signal that hover gives a pointer. **Cue (Brian, Nov 1 2026):** `.hello-cue` fades in over 1s (`ohm-reveal`) at `calc(var(--breathe-delay) + 6s)` = 7.5s, when the first breath's exhale ends, and stays. **Hover glow:** otherwise there is no glow at rest; the full glow (`.omega-glow-wrap`) shows only on hovering the Ω itself (fine pointers; 10R: not the whole page, which is one link), `:focus-visible` (inset ring) and `.is-entering`. The lap (`stroke-dashoffset`, viewBox units inside the svg) and the click pause are unchanged. Only `opacity`, `stroke-dashoffset`, the cue's `text-shadow` transition and the `transform` (`ohm-breathe`) of the line and `.hello-mark` animate. (Step V, Brian, Oct 30 2026: outside `/hello`, the other animations on the site are the H1 divider's `background-position` pulse, `ohm-pulse` / `ohm-pulse-hover`, the dropdown marker, and on Home only the header logo's click spin, `ohm-spin`, which turns only the Ω once counter-clockwise (`rotate(0)` to `rotate(-360deg)`; §A3, §B3 `Header`). `/hello` has no H1 and no header, so it gets none of them. Motion set two (§A3 fifth to tenth exceptions, M1 and M2) also stays off `/hello`, except the page transition when the click pause navigates to Home.) Reduced motion: no light, no glow pulse, no breathing (line or `.hello-mark`), the line and the cue shown statically at once. The Ω is `min(75vmin, 42rem)` wide (10A, was `min(50vmin, 28rem)`), and the line (capitals, wide tracking, cream at 75%) is sized and tracked to span exactly the Ω's ink width (`steps/10A-review-contracts.md` → Line).
- **Indexing:** `noindex` from the page's own `noindex` prop, so it holds after `indexable` turns true. Self canonical. Not in the sitemap, never linked from any page. Not disallowed in robots.txt by name (pre-launch the whole site is disallowed; after launch it's `Allow: /`). `npm run check:dist` enforces all of this in CI.
- **Trailing slash:** `public/hello/index.html` meta-refreshes `/hello/` to `/hello`, because Pages 404s trailing slashes on `build.format: 'file'` pages.
- **Contrast:** the line and the cue (cream 75% into `--bg-dark`) are 6.66:1 on `--bg-dark`, and must stay ≥ 4.5:1 over the art. The cue sits in the Ω's hollow, never on its fill (on `--accent` it would be 1.89:1); the architect checked at 375 and 1280px on Nov 1 2026 that no part of its box touches the fill.

**One source:** `src/data/client-policies.ts` (§B2). The page renders it; the PDF is the doc kit's branded build of the same text (I-043; until then it was printed from the page). - **Page:** `src/pages/client-policies.astro` on `Base` (header, footer, `noindex` while `indexable` is false, like every page).
