  - **Blocks:** `paragraph` → `<p>`; `bullets` → `<ul>`, each `<li>` `<strong>{lead}</strong> {text}` when there is a lead; `table` → `<table>` with `<caption class="visually-hidden">`, `<th scope="col">` head, the first cell of each row a `<th scope="row">`, `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`; `notice` → `<div class="notice">` with two `<div>`s, each a bold `<p>` head then a `<p>` text, side by side from `48rem`, stacked below, 1px `--line-light` border and `--radius`. A `Run` with `href` → `<a>` (same tab; `mailto:` via `mailHref`).
  - **Controls:** `.btn--quiet` is cream-on-transparent (made for dark), so on the cream band the page scopes `color` and `border-color` to `var(--text-on-light)`, and on hover `background: var(--text-on-light)`, `color: var(--bg-light)`. Side by side with `--s-2` gap, `--s-6` above the first section.
  - **Summary:** native disclosure, works with JS off. The `<h2>` sits inside `<summary>` (allowed: summary may hold one heading); keep the browser marker or a CSS chevron from tokens (no hex). No interactive element inside `<summary>`: the anchor link is the body's first child, top right, so it shows only when the section is open.
  - **Anchors:** `id` on the `<details>`. With JS off a `#id` URL scrolls to the closed section. `:target` gets no special style.
- **`src/scripts/policies.ts`** (client script 2; the others are `book.ts`, on Home `logo-spin.ts`, and on the map pages `terrain.ts`; imported only by this page): un-hides `.policies-controls`; `expand` / `collapse` set `open` on every `details.policy`; on load and on `hashchange`, if `location.hash` names a `details.policy`, sets it `open` and scrolls it into view; `beforeprint` opens every section and `afterprint` restores the ones that were closed. No storage, no console, no network, no URL changes of its own.
- **Print stylesheet** (`@media print` in the page's `<style>`; `:global()` for chrome it doesn't own): hide `.site-header`, `.site-footer`, `.skip-link`, `.policies-pdf`, `.policies-controls`, `.policy__anchor`, the BookCta section and the summary marker; show `.print-only`; every surface `background: none`, all text and links `color: var(--ink)` (the green band would print cream on white otherwise); no section padding beyond `--s-4`; `h2 { break-after: avoid }`, tables, the notice and list items `break-inside: avoid`; body at 11pt. No hex.
- **PDF** (I-043): `public/ohm-client-policies.pdf` is the doc kit's branded PDF (letterhead, `Effective: <Month D, YYYY> Version <v>`, its own page footer), saved by Brian and committed (`.gitattributes` marks `*.pdf binary`). The print stylesheet stays for visitors who print the page. **Text check** (`tests/client-policies.test.ts` test 8, devDependency `unpdf`): extract the PDF's text, normalise it (curly quotes to straight, a word split at a hyphen across lines rejoined, whitespace collapsed) and assert that every sentence of every unit of `clientPolicies` (intro, titles, paragraphs, bullets with their lead, table head and rows joined by spaces, notice heads and texts) is in it; both I-037 sentences; `Version {version}` and the long-form date; no phone pattern, no email but `site.email` (so no Zelle address), no placeholder (`TODO`, `TBD`, `XX`, `Drafting`, brackets or braces), no "home visit/office/mobile", no `tel:`/`sms:` link; under 400 KB, starts `%PDF-`. Sequence: a copy of the source with one bullet changed leaves exactly one sentence missing. Failures say to rebuild the PDF in the doc kit. The check covers the words, not the layout: open the PDF after replacing it.
- **Links in:** footer (§A4), Services, Pricing and `/book` (copy deck → Client Policies). Sitemap: yes (§B7).

### B10. Events framework and RSVP (I-048, I-049, I-050; Brian's answers I-060–I-066; Nov 6, 2026; Marea's review I-077–I-080, Nov 7, 2026; I-085, I-086, I-082, I-084, Nov 7, 2026; I-087, Nov 8, 2026; I-088–I-105, Nov 8, 2026: E8–E11 at the end of this section, which win where they differ from the text above)
**Rule: an event is data.** A new event is an entry in `src/data/events.ts`, its images in `src/assets/events/<slug>/` and its copy in the copy deck → Events. No new page, component, script or Apps Script code. Steps: `steps/E1-events-page.md` (data, page, calendar file, feed), `steps/E2-rsvp-form.md` (form and client), `steps/E3-rsvp-script.md` (Apps Script, runbook), `steps/E4-launch-party-edits.md` (description, credits, schedule links, H1, notice and banner styling, privacy line), `steps/E6-self-care-tips.md` (the tips: Apps Script, status reply, tip card, reminder line; built before E5 because of the Nov 21 reminder), `steps/E5-launch-party-edits-2.md` (transparent logos, two-line credits, banner fills the column, section headings, guest card gap, schedule notes), `steps/E7-gmail-sender.md` (I-087: every script mail through `GmailApp` from the events alias; a new permission screen; must be live before the Nov 21 reminder), then E8–E11 (end of this section). First event: the launch party at `/launch-party`, at `/events/launch-party` from E8 (I-092).

**Data (`src/data/events.ts`, CONTRACT).** No imports (tests load it under Node's type stripping, like `client-policies.ts`: no `enum`, `namespace` or parameter properties); image fields are paths, resolved by `src/lib/event-assets.ts`. Copy is the copy deck's, verbatim.
```ts
export type Iso = string;  // '2026-11-22T14:00:00-07:00': local wall time plus the UTC offset in force in timeZone on that date
export type Run = string | { text: string; href: string } | { w: string };   // (E4) plain text · an external link · w(key)
export type Rich = string | Run[];
export interface TimelineItem { start: Iso; end?: Iso; title: string; notes?: Rich[]; optional?: boolean }   // notes Rich since E4
export interface InfoBlock { id: string; title: string; text?: Rich; items?: string[]; inReminder?: boolean }   // text Rich since E8 (I-093)
export interface Notice { id: string; title: string; text: string; link?: { label: string; url: string }; inEmails?: boolean;
                          inResult?: boolean }                // (E9, I-096) its link is also a button on the result card, Going and Maybe
export interface CappedSession { key: string; label: string; item: number; limit: number; waitlist: boolean }
      // label 'Yoga'; item = index into timeline (its time goes in the question); limit and waitlist per I-050
export interface RsvpMail { name: string; thanks?: string; host?: string }   // (E13) the event's words in the emails (Emails below)
export interface EventRsvp { closesAt: Iso; maxGuests: number; reminderAt: Iso; showGoing: boolean; session?: CappedSession;
                             tips?: boolean;                  // (E6) true: the tip card and the reminder tip line (Tips below)
                             mail?: RsvpMail }                // (E13) absent: {eventName} is title, no thanks sentence, no host
export interface Credit { name: string; role: string; url: string; image: string; alt: string;
                          logo?: boolean }                    // (E4; logo E5) logo: transparent, no frame; absent: a framed photo
export interface SiteEvent {
  slug: string; title: string; summary: string;               // title: the full name (meta, preview, .ics, feed, emails); summary: second sentence of the meta description
  heading?: string;                                           // (E4) the on-page H1 when it differs from title
  start: Iso; end: Iso; timeZone: string;                     // 'America/Denver'
  venue: { name: string; address: string };                   // a public venue only, never the office
  description?: Rich[];                                       // (E4) paragraphs under the hero
  timeline: TimelineItem[]; info: InfoBlock[]; notices: Notice[];
  credits?: { heading: string; items: Credit[] };             // (E4) the last section; replaces `host` (removed)
  graphics: { wide: string; narrow: string; og: string; alt: string;      // paths under src/assets/events/; alt (was ogAlt): the graphic's words
              wideMark?: string };                            // (E11, I-104) JSON from `npm run event-banner`: the traced mark over `wide` from 48rem
  index: boolean;                                             // false: noindex and out of the sitemap
  rsvp?: EventRsvp;                                           // absent: no form, no feed
}
export const events: SiteEvent[];                            // (E8) = eventsAt(build time); E8–E11 below
export function launchParty(limit: number, chaiNote?: string | null): SiteEvent;   // (E8, I-091) chaiNote: the event-day swap
export const CHAI_AT: Iso; export const CHAI_NOTE: string | null; export function eventsAt(nowMs: number): SiteEvent[];   // (E8)
export const rsvpText: Record<RsvpTextKey, string>;          // copy deck → Events → RSVP text; keys listed there (E6 adds tipTitle, tipNext, reminderTip)
export const eventHeadings: { description: 'Description'; schedule: 'Schedule'; details: 'Details' };  // (E5) as const; every event page's section H2s
export function eventBySlug(slug: string): SiteEvent | undefined;
```
- **Launch party values** (copy deck → Events → Launch party has every string): slug `launch-party`; `start` `2026-11-22T14:00:00-07:00`, `end` `2026-11-22T18:00:00-07:00` (MST; DST ended Nov 1, 2026); venue CityROCK; `index: false` (decided, I-063: hidden for now, noindex, out of the sitemap, not linked; a Home link may come later as its own Item); `rsvp`: `closesAt` = `start`, `maxGuests` 10 (I-060: Brian sets no limit on +1s; 10 is a hidden technical ceiling against bots, see RSVP form), `reminderAt` `2026-11-21T10:00:00-07:00` (I-061: Sat Nov 21, 10:00 am), `showGoing: false`, `session` `{ key: 'yoga', label: 'Yoga', item: 1, limit: 20, waitlist: true }`. The timeline note `Limited to first 20 sign-ups` is built from `limit` (a const in the file), never typed twice. **E4 (I-077–I-079):** `heading` `A Celebration of Self-Care` (`title` stays the full name); `description` four paragraphs (P1 carries `{ w: 'launchStateTest' }`, P2 a link on `Britt`); timeline notes with one link (`Day pass purchase required`); `credits` four entries; `host` removed; `graphics.alt` (was `ogAlt`). **E5 (I-085, I-086):** credit roles `Host`, `Venue`, `Yoga instruction`, `Graphic design`; CityROCK and JohnMark `logo: true`; item 2's notes end `Activities and merch`, `Optional Tai Chi by John Marshall` (a sibling bullet; no nesting in `notes`); item 3's second note `Harness and shoe rentals available`. **E6 (I-082, I-084):** `rsvp.tips: true`.
- **Guards (build fails, tests too):** slugs match `^[a-z0-9-]{1,40}$`, are unique, and are not in `RESERVED_SLUGS` (every top-level name in `src/pages/` and `public/`, plus `events`, `_astro`, `index`, `404`); `end > start`; every timeline `start` and `rsvp` time carries an explicit offset and that offset is the one `timeZone` uses on that date (`Intl`); `session.item` indexes a timeline item; `showGoing: true` throws `showGoing has no design yet (I-049): decide what it shows first`. **E4:** every link `href` in `description` and timeline notes, and every credit `url`, starts with `https://` (else `event "<slug>": link "<href>" must be https`); every `{ w }` key is a key of `wording` in `src/data/wording.ts` (else `event "<slug>": unknown wording key "<key>"`); a `credits` entry has a non-empty `name`, `role` and `image`.
- **Licensure inside event copy (E4, §A6):** event strings never contain "licensed", "LMT", "massage therapist" or "massage therapy" themselves; a licensure clause is a `{ w }` piece whose unlicensed variant drops the claim (`launchStateTest` = `['', ' and passed his state test to become a licensed neuromuscular massage therapist']`, so unlicensed P1 reads `… 650 hours of studies! 🎉 …`).
- **Emoji:** allowed in event copy (no rule forbids them; Brian's description has 🎉 and ⚡). They are plain characters from the visitor's system font (DM Sans has none); screen readers name them.

**Helpers (`src/lib/events.ts`, pure, Node-tested).**
- `dateLabel(iso, tz)` → `Sunday, Nov 22, 2026`. `timeLabel(start, end?, tz, minutes: 'always' | 'auto')` → `2:00–6:00 pm` (`always`, the hero) or `2–3 pm`, `1:45 pm`, `11:30 am–1 pm` (`auto`, the timeline): lowercase am/pm, an en dash, the meridiem once when both ends share it. `Intl` puts U+202F (narrow no-break space) before AM/PM in current ICU: normalise it to a plain space.
- `mapsUrl(venue)` → `https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&` + `URLSearchParams({ query: name + ', ' + address })` (Maps URLs need no key; [Google](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/urls/get-started), read Nov 6, 2026).
- `icsFor(event, siteUrl, now)` → RFC 5545 text, CRLF lines folded at 75 octets: `VCALENDAR` (`VERSION:2.0`, `PRODID:-//Ohm Precision Bodywork//Events//EN`, `CALSCALE:GREGORIAN`, `METHOD:PUBLISH`) with one `VEVENT`: `UID:<slug>@<site host>`, `DTSTAMP` (`now`, UTC), `DTSTART`/`DTEND` in UTC (`20261122T210000Z` / `20261123T010000Z`), `SUMMARY` title, `LOCATION` venue name and address, `URL` and `DESCRIPTION` the page URL; `,` `;` `\` and newlines escaped ([RFC 5545](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5545) §3.1, §3.3.11).
- `feedFor(event, siteUrl)` → the feed object below. `RESERVED_SLUGS`.

**Routes.**
- `src/pages/events/[event].astro` (**E8, I-092**: moved from `src/pages/[event].astro`): `getStaticPaths` from `events` → `/events/launch-party` (`dist/events/launch-party.html`); `/launch-party` is a redirect page (E8–E11 → Routes). `Base` with `title` `{event.title} · Ohm Precision Bodywork`, `description` `{dateLabel}, {timeLabel always} at {venue.name}. {summary}`, `ogImage` = `graphics.og`, `ogAlt` = `graphics.ogAlt`, `noindex = !event.index` (so it is `noindex` even with `indexable` true; the robots meta stays on while `indexable` is false). Not linked from any page or the nav (Brian shares the URL; decided, I-063); a link from Home may be added later (a new Item).
- `src/pages/events/[slug].ics.ts` → `dist/events/<slug>.ics`, `Content-Type: text/calendar; charset=utf-8`, every event.
- `src/pages/events/[slug].json.ts` → `dist/events/<slug>.json`, only events with `rsvp`. The **feed** is the one place the Apps Script learns about an event, so a new event or a copy change needs no script change:
  `{ v: 1, slug, title, start, end, closesAt, reminderAt, maxGuests, dateLabel, timeLabel, venue: { name, address }, pageUrl, icsUrl, session: { key, label, limit, waitlist, time } | null, reminderInfo: [{ title, text?, items? }] (info blocks with inReminder), notices: [{ title, text, url? }] (notices with inEmails), tips: boolean (E6: rsvp.tips === true), sender: { name: site.name, from: site.eventsEmail, replyTo: site.eventsEmail, contact: site.email }, bookUrl, mail: { name, thanks, host }, signature: { name, credentials, business, url, label }, text: rsvpText }`. **E13:** `bookUrl` = the site root + `/book`; `mail` = `rsvp.mail` with defaults (`name` → `title`, `thanks` and `host` → `''`); `signature` = `{ name: site.owner, credentials: wording.postNominals[licensed ? 1 : 0], business: site.name, url: the site root, label: its host }`. No phone number is ever in the feed: the script reads the numbers from Script Properties at send time. Public facts only: never guest data, `showGoing` or anything not on the page. `v` stays 1: `tips` is an added key the E3 script ignores. **`sender` (E7, I-087):** `from` is the From address of every script mail (the events alias, Mail below); `replyTo` is now the same alias (was `site.email`), so a guest's reply lands under the alias, where Brian can filter it, and matches the From they see; `contact` is Ohm's public contact address (`site.email`): the spot-freed note goes to it and the script's server-error page links it, as the site's own `errServer` line does. The E6 script reads only `name` and `replyTo`, so between the site deploy and the paste it keeps working (replies and the spot-freed note go to the alias, which is Brian's mailbox). These are the feed's only `@` addresses: two distinct, both public (`secrets-scan: allow` in `site.ts`), never in `apps-script/`.

**Page (sections in order; tokens only, no hex, no new token; no motion beyond the H1 pulse and the site-wide exceptions). Bands alternate green and cream from the hero to the footer (E4).**
1. `.section` (green, first): `EventHero` (`event`). A `<picture>`: `graphics.wide` from `48rem`, `graphics.narrow` below (art direction as on About; `getImage` avif + webp; explicit `width`/`height`, so no CLS; **`alt={graphics.alt}`** (E4: the H1 no longer repeats the graphic's words; was `alt=""`)), then the H1 (**`heading ?? title`**, E4), then `<p>` `<time datetime={start}>{dateLabel}</time> · {timeLabel always}`, then `<p>` the venue name and address as one link to `mapsUrl` (`target="_blank" rel="noopener"`), then two buttons: `RSVP` (`.btn`, `href="#rsvp"`, only when `rsvp`) and `Add to calendar` (`.btn btn--quiet`, `href(/events/<slug>.ics)`, `download`). **Wide banner, full column (E5, I-085, Brian: "fill column"; replaces E4's centred 60rem 11:4 crop):** at `min-width: 48rem` only, the `<picture>` is `display: block; overflow: hidden; aspect-ratio: 31 / 10; width: 100%` (no `max-width`, no `margin-inline: auto`: it is the container's full content width, so its left edge is the H1's left edge), and its `img` is `width: 100%; height: 100%; max-width: none; margin-inline: 0; object-fit: cover; object-position: 50% 50%; scale: 1.6129`. On `header-green.png` (1000×450; art, Ω to the end of LAUNCH/PARTY, x 214–784, y 143–307, centred at 50% 50%): `cover` fits the width and keeps rows 63.7–386.3 (1000 / 3.1 = 322.6 rows); `scale` 1.6129 (= 1000 / 620) about the centre then shows source x 190–810, y 125–325 (620×200), so the art has 24 / 26 source px of margin left / right and 18 top and bottom. Sizes: at the full container (viewport ≥ 72rem) the box is 70rem = 1120×361 CSS px, 1.81 CSS px per source px (E4: 1.45 at 960 px, so the words read about 25% larger than E4); at 48rem it is about 736×237 (1.19). **Sharpness:** the 1000 px file is upscaled by the browser up to 1.81x (3.6 device px per source px on a 2x screen), so edges soften, most visibly on the thin `PRECISION BODYWORK` letters; there is no larger file. `widths` stay `[wide.width]` (one 1000w candidate: the 500w file would be upscaled 3.6x) and `sizes` becomes `(min-width: 72rem) 70rem, calc(100vw - 2rem)` (the slot width). A 2x export from JohnMark (2000×900, open since E4) would fix it with no CSS change: replace the file in place (the crop is in percentages); then the link preview grows to 1200×630 and `tests/events.test.ts` 9a's 857×450 changes. Below `48rem` the narrow mark is unchanged (max 24rem, uncropped, centred). The link preview stays the full graphic (`graphics.og`, `Base` crop unchanged).
2. `.section.band-light`: `EventDescription` (E4, only when `description`: **E5:** `<h2>{eventHeadings.description}</h2>`, then one `<p>` per paragraph through `EventRich`, `--s-6` from the H2 to the first paragraph (as the Schedule H2 to its list), max width `--measure`, `--s-4` between paragraphs, `margin-bottom: var(--s-12)`), then `EventTimeline` (H2 **`{eventHeadings.schedule}`** (E5; was typed in the component), `<ol class="timeline">`; each `<li>` holds `<time datetime={start}>{timeLabel auto}</time>`, an `<h3>` title and a `<ul>` of notes, each through `EventRich`; a vertical 2px `--line-light` rule with a 10px square `--accent` marker per item, hollow (`--accent` 2px border, `--bg-light` fill) when `optional`; times `tabular-nums`, weight 600; time beside the text from `48rem`, above it below). (E1's `EventHost` is deleted in E4.)
3. `.section` (green, only when `info` is not empty): **E5 (I-085):** `<h2>{eventHeadings.details}</h2>` (in `[event].astro`, read from the data), then `EventInfo` for each `info` block: **`<h3>`** (was `<h2>`) and a `<p>` (`text`) or `<ul>` (`items`), `--s-2` from the H3 to its text. `EventInfo`'s scoped CSS: `.event-info { margin-top: var(--s-6) }` (H2 to the first block) and `.event-info + .event-info { margin-top: var(--s-8) }`. The block `id`s (`wear`, `parking`, `raffle`) stay. **Outline after E5:** H1 · H2 Description · H2 Schedule (H3 items) · H2 Details (H3 blocks) · H2 RSVP (H3 result title; E6 adds the H3 tip title) · H2 notice title · H2 credits heading; no skipped level (Lighthouse `heading-order`).
4. `.section.band-light#rsvp` (E2): `RsvpForm` (only when `rsvp`).
5. `.section` (green): `EventNotice` for each notice ("shown lower on the page", I-048). **E4 (I-080), a light box on the green band:** `background: var(--bg-light)`, `color: var(--text-on-light)`, `border: 1px solid var(--green-300)`, `border-top: 3px solid var(--accent)`, `--radius`, `--s-6` padding, `max-width: var(--measure)`; its link `color: var(--link-on-light)`; `<h2>` title, `<p>` text, `<p>` link (`target="_blank" rel="noopener"`, the copy deck's label). Pairs: ink on cream 14.3:1, green-700 on cream 8.1:1 (E4 adds this pair to `check:contrast`).
6. `.section.band-light` (E4, I-079, only when `credits`): `EventCredits`. `<h2>{credits.heading}</h2>`, then `<ul class="credits">` (`list-style: none`, `padding: 0`, `margin-top: var(--s-6)`, `display: grid`, `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(15rem, 1fr))`, `gap: var(--s-6)`), one `<li>` per entry holding one `<a href={url} target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="credit">` with the image (`<Image>` from `eventAsset(image)`, `height={56}`, `densities={[1, 2]}`, `formats={['avif', 'webp']}`, `alt={alt}`; CSS `display: block; height: 3.5rem; width: auto; max-width: 100%; object-fit: contain; object-position: left center`; **E5:** the photo frame `border: 1px solid var(--line-light); border-radius: var(--radius)` only on photos, through `class:list={['credit__img', { 'credit__img--photo': !credit.logo }]}` on the `<Image>` and the border rule on `.credit :global(.credit__img--photo)`; a `logo: true` image has no border and no radius, its transparent pixels show the cream band), then **(E5, I-085)** `<span class="credit__text"><strong class="credit__name">{name}</strong>{' '}<span class="credit__role">{role}</span></span>`: `.credit__text { display: block; margin-top: var(--s-2) }`, `.credit__name { display: block }`, `.credit__role { display: block; font-size: var(--fs-small) }`. No comma; the `{' '}` keeps a space in the text so the link's name reads `CityROCK Venue`, not `CityROCKVenue`. Name and role stay inside the one link (both underlined, `--link-on-light`); the link's name is `alt` + name + role. Four across at 1280 px, one per row at 375 px.
`EventHero`, `EventDescription`, `EventTimeline`, `EventInfo`, `EventNotice` and `EventCredits` take the event (or one block) as their only prop and type no copy. **`EventRich`** (E4) takes `text: Rich` and renders inline content only (no wrapper element): a string as text; `{ text, href }` as `<a href={href} target="_blank" rel="noopener">{text}</a>`; `{ w }` as `w(key)` (imports `src/data/wording.ts`).

**RSVP form (`RsvpForm`, E2).** Works without JS: `<form method="post" action={site.rsvpUrl}>` with hidden `slug` and `mode=html`; the Apps Script answers with its own page and a link back. Fields (`name` attributes are the wire contract, shared by `src/lib/rsvp.ts` and the script):
| Field | Name | Values |
|---|---|---|
| Name | `name` | 1–80 characters after trim |
| Email | `email` | ≤ 254, `^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$`; stored trimmed and lowercased |
| Are you coming? | `status` | `going` · `maybe` · `cant` |
| Session question (when `session`) | `session` | `yes` · `no`; required unless `cant` |
| Guest n (n = 1…`maxGuests`) | `g{n}name`, `g{n}session`, `g{n}email` | **Brian, Nov 9, 2026:** `g{n}email` is optional (label `guestEmail`, placeholder `guestEmailHint`); when typed it follows the `email` rule (trimmed, lowercased, ≤ 254, same regex), else the field `g{n}email` is invalid (`errGuestEmail`); the row is blank (dropped) only when name, answer and email are all blank; it is stored in that guest's row `Email` cell and gets the guest email (§Emails). A row with a blank name and no answer is dropped; a name needs an answer and an answer needs a name; dropped entirely when `cant`; `g{n}` above `maxGuests` is ignored. **E4 (I-078):** each guest's session yes/no has a **visible** `<legend>` with the filled `sessionQuestion` (`Joining yoga (2–3 pm)?`), the same string as the RSVPer's own question (was `visually-hidden`); no new string |
| News opt-in (I-065) | `optin` | a checkbox, `value="yes"`, never `checked` by default; `yes` → opted in, anything else or absent → not; shown for every status (not hidden by `cant`); label `rsvpText.optIn`; it gates news and offers, and (E4, I-078) invitations to future events, which count as Ohm news; never event emails for this event (Privacy) |
| Honeypot | `website` | must be empty; in a `.visually-hidden` wrapper with `aria-hidden="true"`, `tabindex="-1"`, `autocomplete="off"` |
Form order: intro, spots line, name, email, status, session question, guests (`Add a guest` under the rows), the opt-in checkbox, the submit button, then the `privacy` line as the form's last child (`<p class="rsvp-privacy">`, so it hides with the form on success). **`maxGuests` is a hidden ceiling** (I-060): no text ever states it, and nothing tells the visitor a limit exists; it only caps how many rows exist and how many the script reads. `RsvpForm` renders all `maxGuests` rows; `NOJS_GUEST_ROWS = 3` (in `src/lib/rsvp.ts`): rows 1–3 show and rows 4…`maxGuests` carry `hidden`, so without JS three optional rows show (a no-JS visitor with more guests replies to the confirmation email), and `name`, `email` and `status` carry `required`. **With JS** (`src/scripts/rsvp.ts`, client script 5, imported only by `RsvpForm`): sets `mode=json` and `novalidate`; hides the session fieldset and guests while `cant` is checked; hides every guest row, then shows them one at a time (`Add a guest` reveals the next row and is hidden once row `maxGuests` shows, with no message; `Remove guest n` clears and hides the row); validates with `validateRsvp` (copy deck messages, `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, focus the first bad field); posts with `fetch(site.rsvpUrl, { method: 'POST', body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` and a 15 s `AbortController` timeout; while sending, the button is disabled and reads `Sending…`; on success, hides the form and shows the result in `<div class="rsvp-result" role="status" tabindex="-1">` (focused): the title, the line, a list `<name> · <outcome>` for you and each guest, `maybeNote` when any outcome is `maybe`, and the `Add to calendar` button; on a `pending` reply (the email already has an RSVP), `changeTitle` and `changeText` only; then re-reads spots. On load it GETs `site.rsvpUrl?slug=<slug>` and fills `<p class="rsvp-spots" aria-live="polite" hidden>` above the form; if that fails it stays hidden (the timeline already says `Limited to first 20 sign-ups`). After `closesAt` (client clock) it hides the form and shows the closed line. Copy reaches the script in `data-text` (JSON of `rsvpText`) on the form, not a `<script type="application/json">`. No storage, no cookies, no console, no URL change, no request except to `site.rsvpUrl`.
- **Guest card spacing (E5, I-086, Marea: "a little bit of space between the name box and the yoga? Yes or no selection"):** in each guest card the name is a `span.field` and the yoga question the next sibling `fieldset.group`, so E2's `.guest .group + .group` never matched and the two touched. Replace that rule with `.guest .field + .group { margin-top: var(--s-4); }` (16 px, the card's own padding). The RSVPer's own fields sit in the form's `grid` with `gap: var(--s-6)`, so their yoga question already has space; no change there.
- **Tip card (E6, I-082; JS only).** Markup in `RsvpForm`, a sibling **after** `.rsvp-result` (not inside it: `role="status"` is implicitly `aria-atomic`, so a tip change inside it would re-read the whole result): `<div class="rsvp-tip" hidden><h3 class="rsvp-tip__title">{t.tipTitle}</h3><p class="rsvp-tip__text" aria-live="polite"></p><button type="button" class="link-button rsvp-tip__next" hidden>{t.tipNext}</button></div>`. Without JS it stays `hidden` (the no-JS reply page is the script's and shows no tip). CSS: `.rsvp-tip { margin-top: var(--s-6); padding: var(--s-6); border: 1px solid var(--line-light); border-radius: var(--radius) }`, `.rsvp-tip > * + * { margin-top: var(--s-3) }`; no accent edge (the result keeps it), no transition or animation, existing tokens only (ink on cream and `--link-on-light` on cream, both already in `check:contrast`). **Logic** (`src/lib/rsvp.ts`, pure): `parseStatus` adds `tips: string[]` to its ok reply, from `cleanTips(o.tips)` (a missing or malformed `tips` gives `[]` and never fails the status); `cleanTips(raw: unknown): string[]` keeps strings only, replaces control characters with a space, collapses whitespace, trims, drops empties and anything over `TIP_MAX = 280` characters, drops case-insensitive duplicates (first kept), keeps the first `TIPS_MAX = 100`; `shuffle<T>(list: T[], random: () => number): T[]` (Fisher–Yates, a new array); `tipDeck(tips: string[], random: () => number): { size: number; next(): string }`: a shuffled order, `next()` walks it, and when it runs out reshuffles, and if the new first equals the tip just shown (size > 1) swaps it with the last, so there is no repeat until all are seen and never the same tip twice in a row. `createRsvp` gains `random?: () => number` (default `Math.random`), state `tip: string | null` and `moreTips: boolean`, and `nextTip(): void`. The deck is built from the first non-empty `tips` a status read returns (on load or the re-read after a send) and kept for the page view; whenever `result` is set (any ok reply, `pending`, `cant`, or the honeypot's quiet success) and a deck exists and `tip` is null, `tip = deck.next()` and `moreTips = deck.size > 1`; a deck that arrives with the post-send re-read fills the card then. No tips, a failed read or an empty list: `tip` stays null and the card stays hidden; the RSVP is unaffected. **DOM** (`src/scripts/rsvp.ts`): `card.hidden = !s.result || !s.tip`; `text.textContent = s.tip ?? ''` (never `innerHTML`); `button.hidden = !s.moreTips`; a click calls `rsvp.nextTip()`, focus stays on the button and the live region announces the new tip. The first tip is not announced on its own (focus goes to the result, as now); the visitor reads on to it.
- **Why form-urlencoded, never JSON** (probed Nov 6, 2026 against the placeholder deployment): the web app answers `OPTIONS` with 200 and no CORS headers, so a request that needs a preflight (e.g. `Content-Type: application/json`) fails. A `URLSearchParams` body with no custom headers is a CORS-simple request: no preflight. The `/exec` reply is a `302` to `script.googleusercontent.com/macros/echo…` ([Google: Content Service](https://developers.google.com/apps-script/guides/content), read Nov 6, 2026); both legs send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, and `fetch` follows a 302 on POST as a GET ([Fetch standard](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-redirect-fetch)). An Apps Script error comes back as an HTML page: anything that isn't the JSON below counts as `server`.
- **`site.rsvpUrl`** (E2, in `site.ts`): `https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbztJsWy8MhhaQXrMIfGBtxM8ZpqGIrBcGaZcO_ZWRmNhbwCm8_3epqZYg1yY18Nvb6N/exec`. Public (Brian, I-049); one deployment serves every event; updating the script keeps the URL (Manage deployments → Edit → New version, [Google](https://developers.google.com/apps-script/concepts/deployments), read Nov 6, 2026). If that placeholder is not a standalone project in the Ohm Workspace account (I-062, and see Apps Script below), I-058 deploys a new one there and this URL changes once (a one-line `site.ts` Item).

**Wire contract (the script's replies, JSON; the client and the tests share it).**
- `GET ?slug=` → `{ ok: true, open: boolean, session: { spotsLeft: number, full: boolean, waitlist: boolean } | null, tips: string[] }` or `{ ok: false, error: 'unknown' }`. **`tips` (E6, I-082):** always present on an ok reply; the cleaned tips (Tips below) when the feed says `tips: true`, else `[]`; also `[]` when `TIPS_SHEET_ID` is unset, the sheet can't be read or has no tips. A reply from the E3 script has no `tips`; the client reads that as `[]`.
- `POST` (a new email for this event) → `{ ok: true, status, outcomes: Outcome[] }` with `Outcome = 'confirmed' | 'waitlist' | 'full' | 'maybe' | 'no'` (`maybe`: a yes-answer under status `maybe`, which holds no spot, I-064), one per person in order (you, then each kept guest), `[]` for `cant` or an event without a session.
- `POST` (the email already has an RSVP for this event) → `{ ok: true, status, pending: true, outcomes: [] }`: nothing is changed; a confirm-change link went to that address (see Changes). The reply is the same whether or not the email was sent (throttle). **Brian, Nov 9, 2026:** the same reply when only a guest row holds the address (Changes → Guest requests), so the reply never says which.
- `POST` errors → `{ ok: false, error: 'invalid' | 'closed' | 'unknown' | 'busy' | 'server', fields?: string[] }` (`fields` = wire names, e.g. `['email', 'g2session']`). `duplicate` is gone (I-064); a reply carrying it is not valid, so the client reads it as `server`.
- `GET ?change=<token>` and `POST change=<token>` answer with `HtmlService` pages only (the email link's pages; never JSON, never read by the site's client).
- **Never** in any JSON reply: an email address, any name (outcomes are tokens; the client pairs them with the names it holds), a count other than `spotsLeft`, a sheet or script ID (`SHEET_ID` or `TIPS_SHEET_ID`), a change token, the opt-in answer. The tips are public content by design (Privacy). The no-JS response page and the change pages may show the names in that submission, never names stored in the sheet.

**Apps Script (`apps-script/rsvp.js`, CONTRACT, E3).** Plain V8 script, no `export`, helpers end in `_` (Apps Script hides them from the Run menu). It runs in the **Ohm Workspace account** (I-062) as a **standalone** project (script.google.com → New project, not Extensions → Apps Script from the sheet): Google sets `allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation` on the `HtmlService` sandbox only for standalone projects, and the change page's Confirm button needs it ([HTML restrictions](https://developers.google.com/apps-script/guides/html/restrictions), read Nov 6, 2026). Every link and form on a script page carries `target="_top"` (same page: links in the IFRAME sandbox need `_top` or `_blank`). Brian pastes it into `Code.gs` and `appsscript.json` (`timeZone` `America/Denver`, `runtimeVersion` `V8`, `webapp` `{ access: 'ANYONE_ANONYMOUS', executeAs: 'USER_DEPLOYING' }`, [manifest](https://developers.google.com/apps-script/manifest/web-app-api-executable), read Nov 6, 2026; no `oauthScopes`, so Apps Script detects them; E7 adds the Gmail scope, Mail below), sets one Script Property, `SHEET_ID` (E6 adds an optional second, `TIPS_SHEET_ID`, Tips below), runs `setup()` once, and updates the existing deployment (I-058). The repo holds no sheet ID, script ID, guest data or email address; `SITE_ORIGIN = 'https://ohmprecisionbodywork.com'` is the only constant.
- **Event facts:** `loadEvent_(slug)`: slug must match `^[a-z0-9-]{1,40}$`; `UrlFetchApp.fetch(SITE_ORIGIN + '/events/' + slug + '.json', { muteHttpExceptions: true })`, cached 600 s in `CacheService`; not 200 or `v !== 1` → `unknown`.
- **Sheet:** spreadsheet `SHEET_ID`, one tab per event named by slug, created with its header row on the first RSVP. One row per person, columns in this fixed order (the script writes the header and reads by position; Brian adds notes only to the right of the last column): `Submitted` · `Changed` (time of the last confirmed change, else blank) · `RSVP` (an id shared by you and your guests) · `Who` (`you` | `guest`) · `Name` · `Email` (`you` rows only) · `Opt-in` (`yes` | blank; `you` rows only, I-065; gates news, offers and invitations to future events, I-078) · `Status` (`going` | `maybe` | `cant`) · `{session.label}` (`confirmed` | `waitlist` | `full` | `maybe` | `no` | blank) · `Waitlist #` · `Reminder sent`. An RSVP's rows are always written together, and replaced together by a change. Text cells starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` get a leading `'` (no formula injection); control characters are stripped.
- **`doPost(e)`** (`e.parameter`): honeypot filled → the success shape with `outcomes: []`, nothing saved or sent; `loadEvent_`; now ≥ `closesAt` → `closed`; `validate_` (same rules and cases as `validateRsvp`) → `invalid` + `fields`; then **one script lock** (`LockService.getScriptLock().tryLock(20000)`, false → `busy`): read the tab; a `you` row with the same email → the change path below (nothing written in this call); else count `confirmed` and `waitlist` cells in the session column and **assign** each person in order: answer `no` → `no`; `yes` under status `maybe` → `maybe` (holds no spot, I-064); `yes` under `going` → `confirmed` if `confirmed < limit` **and no one is waitlisted**, else `waitlist` (next `Waitlist #`) when `waitlist` is on, else `full`; append all rows in one `setValues` (`Opt-in` = `yes` when `optin` is `yes`); `SpreadsheetApp.flush()`; release in `finally` (Google: flush before releasing, [Lock](https://developers.google.com/apps-script/reference/lock/lock), read Nov 6, 2026). Then, outside the lock, `send_` the confirmation (Mail below: `GmailApp` from E7; E3–E6 used `MailApp.sendEmail`); a mail failure doesn't undo the RSVP. Reply JSON, or with `mode=html` an `HtmlService` page (every interpolated value HTML-escaped) with the result and a `target="_top"` link back to `pageUrl`.
- **`doGet(e)`:** with `slug`, the status reply: `spotsLeft` = 0 while anyone is waitlisted, else `max(0, limit − confirmed)` (`maybe` cells hold nothing); `full` = `spotsLeft === 0`; `open` = now < `closesAt`. Reads without the lock. With `change`, the confirm page (Changes).
- **Changes (I-064: one RSVP per email stays; a repeat RSVP updates it, confirmed from that inbox).** Why: one RSVP per email exists so nobody can make the script email or edit other people's RSVPs; if a repeat submission overwrote directly, anyone who knows a guest's email could change or cancel their RSVP. So a repeat submission changes nothing until the address owner confirms it:
  1. *Request* (`doPost`, the email has an RSVP): after releasing the lock, `token = Utilities.getUuid()`; `CacheService.getScriptCache().put('chg:' + token, JSON {slug, email, base, submission}, 21600)` (`base` = the RSVP's `Changed`, else `Submitted`; `submission` = the validated fields); mail the change email (copy deck → Emails → Change) to the **stored** address, greeting the **stored** name, with `changeUrl` = `ScriptApp.getService().getUrl() + '?change=' + token` ([Service.getUrl](https://developers.google.com/apps-script/reference/script/service), read Nov 6, 2026). Throttle: at most 3 change emails per RSVP per 6 hours (a cache counter under `'chgn:' + base64(SHA-256(slug + ' ' + email))`, since keys are ≤ 250 characters); over it, no mail, same reply. Reply `pending`.
  2. *Confirm page* (`doGet` `change`): token missing or expired → `changeExpired`; now ≥ `closesAt` → `closed`. Else a page: `changeConfirmLead`, `newAnswer`, one `answerLine` per person in the submission (session events, not `cant`), and `<form method="post" action={getUrl()} target="_top">` with hidden `change` and `mode=html` and the `changeConfirm` button. A GET never changes anything (mail scanners open links).
  3. *Apply* (`doPost` `change`): token missing → `changeExpired`; closed → `closed`; under the lock: the RSVP's current `Changed`/`Submitted` ≠ `base` → `changeExpired` (another change won; each token works once and is removed). Then for each person in the submission, the **previous** row is the `you` row for you, and for a guest the first unused old guest row with the same name (trimmed, lowercased; a renamed guest is a new person). A person still `going` + `yes` whose previous cell is `confirmed` or `waitlist` **keeps** it (and the `Waitlist #`), even when the session is full; everyone else is assigned fresh as above, counting every other row in the tab plus the kept cells. Delete the RSVP's old rows (bottom up), append the new ones in one `setValues` with the old `Submitted`, `Changed` = now, the old `Reminder sent`, `Opt-in` from the submission (the latest answer wins). Flush, release. Then mail the normal confirmation or can't-go note for the new state, and, when the change freed any `confirmed` cell while someone is still waitlisted, one spot-freed note to `sender.contact` (Brian; E7, I-087: was `sender.replyTo`; a feed without `contact` falls back to `replyTo`). The page: `changeDoneTitle` with the outcome lines (`cantTitle`/`cantText` for `cant`) and the `target="_top"` back link.
  4. *Guest requests (Brian, Nov 9, 2026: guest self-removal).* In `submit_`, under the lock, an address that matches no `you` row but matches guest rows (`Email` cell) whose RSVP still has its `you` row (`findGuests_`; an orphan guest row is ignored) is a guest request: nothing is written and the reply is `pending`, as in 1. Only on a feed with `guestRemoveLead` (an older feed: a new RSVP, as before). The same throttle counter as 1 (`allowMail_`, per address). The guest's stored name and the RSVPer's stored name are used, never the typed ones. **Going or Maybe:** no token; `mailGuestListed_` (`guestListedSubject`, `guestListedLead`, `guestChangeLine`). **Can't go:** `chg:<token>` = `{ kind: 'guest', slug, email, base: { <RSVP id>: <that you row's Changed or Submitted> } }` for `CHANGE_TTL`; `mailGuestRemove_` to the guest's address (`guestRemoveSubject`, `guestRemoveLead`, `changeLinkLine`, `guestRemoveIgnore`). The confirm page (GET) for a guest token is `guestRemoveConfirmLead` and the same form and button script. *Apply* (`applyGuest_`, from `applyChange_` when `kind` is `guest`, after the closed check): under the lock, re-read the tab; delete (bottom up) each guest row with that address whose RSVP id is in `base` and whose `you` row's base still matches; never the `you` row or another guest; the `you` row is not touched, so its `Changed` stays. None left → the done page or `changeExpired` (stale: a change to that RSVP, a hand deletion, or expiry). Else `chgdone:<token>` = `{ kind: 'guest', slug }` before the lock opens; then one `mailGuestRemoved_` per RSVP to its `you` address (`guestRemovedSubject`, `guestRemovedNote`); `mailSpotFreed_(ev, n)` when n removed rows were `confirmed` and any other row is `waitlist`; the page `guestRemovedTitle` · `guestRemovedText` (also on a second press). The guest gets no email after confirming. A guest who is later re-listed by the RSVPer's own confirmed change is back on the list (the RSVPer's choice; they got the note). No new column, no reminders for guests, no do-not-email list. Tests G-5–G-10.
  **Trade-off, plainly:** a change needs the guest's inbox (one more step, a link valid up to 6 hours; Google's cache may drop it sooner, so the guest just RSVPs again), and the spot is taken or released when they press Confirm, not when they submit; a `maybe` → `going` upgrade at a full session joins the waitlist then. Anyone can still send one email's worth of nuisance to a known address (as a first RSVP already can), capped at 3 per 6 hours; and the `pending` reply tells a stranger that this address has an RSVP for this event, nothing more. In exchange nobody can change, cancel or upgrade another person's RSVP.
- **Freeing a spot is by hand** (I-050): Brian changes a `confirmed` cell to `no` (or deletes the row), then changes the first `waitlist` row (lowest `Waitlist #`) to `confirmed` and emails that guest himself. A guest's own confirmed change can free spots too; the script then emails Brian the spot-freed note and still promotes nobody. Because new yes-answers queue while anyone is waitlisted, a freed spot never jumps the queue.
- **Reminders:** `setup()` deletes any trigger for `sendDueReminders`, logs `MailApp.getRemainingDailyQuota()` (so Brian sees the account's real limit) and creates `ScriptApp.newTrigger('sendDueReminders').timeBased().everyMinutes(15).create()` (allowed: 1, 5, 10, 15, 30, [ClockTriggerBuilder](https://developers.google.com/apps-script/reference/script/clock-trigger-builder), read Nov 6, 2026), so a reminder goes within about 15 minutes after `reminderAt`, with no per-event setup. `sendDueReminders()`: for each tab whose name is a slug, `loadEvent_`; if `reminderAt ≤ now < start`: under the lock, snapshot the `you` rows with status `going` or `maybe` and a blank `Reminder sent`, with each RSVP's people and their current session cells (so Brian's hand edits show), and release; send each reminder while `MailApp.getRemainingDailyQuota() > 0` (E7 keeps this read-only check, Mail below); then under the lock again stamp `Reminder sent` on those RSVP ids. A guest whose session cell is blank (`cant`) gets no line; a `maybe` cell reads `outcomeMaybe`, and an RSVP with any `maybe` cell also gets `maybeNote`. A change keeps `Reminder sent`, so nobody gets a second reminder.
- **Tips (E6, I-082, I-084; Brian's sheet `Self Care tip of the day`, tab `Sheet1`, column A, header `Tip`).** Constants `TIPS_TAB = 'Sheet1'`, `TIPS_TTL = 300`, `TIP_MAX = 280`, `TIPS_MAX = 100`, cache key `'tips'`. **Where the sheet comes from:** `SpreadsheetApp.openById(TIPS_SHEET_ID)`, a Script Property Brian sets himself (the ID from the sheet's address bar; never in the repo, like `SHEET_ID`). Chosen over a Drive lookup by name: `openById` needs only the `spreadsheets` scope the script already has, so no new consent screen ([SpreadsheetApp.openById](https://developers.google.com/apps-script/reference/spreadsheet/spreadsheet-app), read Nov 7, 2026), while `DriveApp.getFilesByName` needs `drive.readonly` or `drive`, access to every file in the account ([DriveApp](https://developers.google.com/apps-script/reference/drive/drive-app), read Nov 7, 2026), and a name can match several files or change. The Ohm Workspace account that runs the script must be able to open the sheet: it owns it, or the owner shares it with that account as Viewer (I-083, Brian's todo). **`readTips_()`:** no `TIPS_SHEET_ID` → `[]` (no sheet call). Else a cache hit on `'tips'` (a JSON array) is returned. Else, inside `try`: open the sheet, take tab `TIPS_TAB` or, if renamed, the first tab, read `getDataRange().getValues()` and keep column A; `cleanTips_` (`str_` each cell, control characters to a space, whitespace collapsed, trimmed; skip a cell equal to `Tip` ignoring case (the header), empties, cells over `TIP_MAX` characters and case-insensitive duplicates, first kept; stop at `TIPS_MAX`); any error gives `[]`. The result, even `[]`, is cached `TIPS_TTL` seconds (`CacheService` values may be up to 100 KB, keys 250 characters, expiry at most 21,600 s, [Cache](https://developers.google.com/apps-script/reference/cache/cache), read Nov 7, 2026; 100 × 280 characters stays well under 100 KB), so Brian's edits reach the site within about 5 minutes with no redeploy, a broken share costs one slow read per 5 minutes, and no request can make the script read the sheet more often. No lock (read only). **Status reply:** `doGet` with `slug` adds `tips: ev.tips === true ? readTips_() : []` after the spots; a tips failure never changes `ok`, `open` or `session`. **Reminder (I-084):** in `remindEvent_`, after the snapshot lock is released and before sending, `deck = ev.tips === true ? tipDeck_(readTips_()) : null` (same walk as the client's `tipDeck`, with `Math.random`: shuffled, reshuffled when used up, no repeat within the run until every tip is used, never the same twice in a row); each due RSVP gets `d.tip = deck && deck.size ? deck.next() : ''`. `mailReminder_` pushes one block `fill_(t.reminderTip, { tip: d.tip })` just before the `signoff` block, only when `d.tip` and `t.reminderTip` are both non-empty (an older feed without `reminderTip`, or no tip, sends the reminder as before). The email is plain text (the `body` argument of `GmailApp.sendEmail` from E7; no `htmlBody`), so the tip goes in as text; if I-081 ever makes it HTML, the tip must go through `esc_`. The position is one line in `mailReminder_` and the words are `rsvpText.reminderTip` from the feed, so I-081 can reword it with a site deploy and move it with a one-line script change. The confirmation, can't-go, change and spot-freed emails never call `readTips_`. **`setup()`** also logs `Tips read: <n>` (0 when `TIPS_SHEET_ID` is unset, with `TIPS_SHEET_ID not set (no tips)`, or when the sheet can't be opened), so Brian sees at once whether the share worked; it never logs a tip or the ID.
- **Emails** (E13: HTML with a plain-text body, except the spot-freed note; strings from `text`, layout in the copy deck → Events → Emails): confirmation (going/maybe), short note (can't go), change link (repeat RSVP), spot-freed note (to Brian), reminder (going/maybe: date and time, address, the `reminderInfo` blocks (what to wear, parking), each person's session status, the notices with their links, the page and calendar links, and from E6 one `reminderTip` line). These go to the RSVPer whatever their `Opt-in` (I-069): they are the "event details and reminders" of the privacy line (I-078; reworded by Brian, Nov 9, 2026); the guest email is its "the same" (Brian, Nov 9, 2026). The script never sends news, offers or invitations to future events. **E13 (Marea's copy, Brian's decisions, Nov 8, 2026):** the confirmation (going and maybe) and the can't-go note are Marea's layout; the change and reminder emails keep their words. All four end with Brian's reply signature (`signature_`) instead of the `signoff` line (removed). *Build:* each mail is a list of blocks, a block a list of lines; a line is a string, `{ head }` (a heading: `<strong style="color:MAIL_GREEN">` in HTML, plain in the text) or `{ runs }` (strings and `{ text, href }` links, made by `tpl_` from a template whose `{key}` is a feed URL; in the text a link whose words aren't its URL puts the URL on the next line). `mail_(ev, blocks)` → `{ text, html }`: text = blocks joined by a blank line plus the plain signature; html = `<div>`, one `<p style="margin:0 0 16px">` per block with `<br>` between lines, then the signature table. Every string is escaped with `esc_`; only feed URLs become links, never a guest's name. *Colours:* `MAIL_GREEN = '#125245'` and `MAIL_TERRA = '#C37A5B'`, named constants in `rsvp.js` (the script can't read `tokens.css`; they are `--green-700` and `--terra-500`, and a test keeps them equal; the no-raw-hex rule is about the site). *Signature:* plain `{owner}, {credentials}` (no comma part when `credentials` is empty) · `business` · `{SIGNATURE_PHONE} • {label}` (no phone: `label` alone, no bullet); HTML: a one-cell table, Arial 12px/16px, `MAIL_GREEN`, left border 2px solid `MAIL_TERRA`, `padding-left:10px`; line 1 bold 13px/17px name with the credentials in a `font-weight:normal` span; line 2 the business, bold, linked to `url`; line 3 the phone as a `tel:` link (digits and `+` only in the href), a `MAIL_TERRA` `&nbsp;&bull;&nbsp;`, then `label` linked to `url`. No image. A feed without `signature` (older than the script) signs with `sender.name` as before. *Phones:* Script Properties `SIGNATURE_PHONE` (Brian) and `HOST_PHONE` (the host), both optional, read through `prop_` (trimmed; `''` when unset or unreadable; [Properties.getProperty](https://developers.google.com/apps-script/reference/properties/properties) returns `null` for a missing key, read Nov 8, 2026) at send time only, never cached, logged or written anywhere. The confirmation's questions line is `questionsHost` when `HOST_PHONE` and `mail.host` are both set, else `questions`. *Yoga lines* (session events only): each person's `sessionAnswer` from their cell: `confirmed` Yes, `waitlist` `sessionWaitlist`, `full`/`no`/`maybe` No; `waitlistNote` after the list when anyone waits; `maybeNote` is no longer in the confirmation (it stays on the pages and in the reminder). **E14 (Brian, Nov 8, 2026), supersedes the *Yoga lines* rule above:** only Going answers the session question (`validateRsvp`/`validate_`: answers sent with a Maybe are dropped; the form hides them via `data-going-only`); a Maybe stores cell `maybe` for every person. The confirmation is `detailsHead` · `yourRsvp` · (Going, session event) `sessionAnswer`, then a `guestsHead` heading and one `{ li }` bullet per guest (`guestLine`, or the name alone for a Maybe/no session); Yes `MAIL_GREEN`, No `MAIL_CTA` (`#9C5739`, `--terra-700`), Waitlist plain (`{ text, tone }` runs). New line kinds: `{ li }` (consecutive ones become one `<ul>`) and `{ button: { text, href } }` (a table-cell button, `MAIL_CTA` fill, `MAIL_CTA_TEXT` `#F3F2F0` = `--cream`, on its own line; text: words then URL). The book block is `bookHead` · the `bookLink` button (Brian, Nov 9, 2026: `bookLine` removed). **Guest email (Brian, Nov 9):** after a Going or Maybe RSVP, `mailOutcome_` sends `mailGuest_(ev, to, guestName, inviter, status, cell)` to each guest address, guest i with `cell = assigned[i + 1].cell` (subject `confirmSubject`). **Brian, Nov 9 (after testing): the confirmation's format.** `confirmBlocks_(ev, name, lead, details, changeLine)` builds both mails: `hi` · lead · details · `[changeLine, pageUrl]` · when/where · `calendarLines_` · `noticeBlocks_` · `bookBlock_` · `questionsLine_` · `seeYou`, then the signature. The guest's lead is `guestLead` (`{inviter}` = the RSVPer's name), its change line `guestChangeLine`, and its details `detailsBlocks_(ev, status, [{ name: guestName }], [{ cell }])`: `detailsHead` · `yourRsvp` · (Going, session event) `sessionAnswer` from the guest's own cell · `waitlistNote` when that cell is `waitlist`; one person, so never `guestsHead`, the RSVPer or another guest (was: when/where, calendar, notices, `detailsLine`, `guestChangeLine`, questions, `seeYou`; no book block, no answers). It skips the RSVPer's address, repeats, and every address any row of the event's tab held before this write (`emailsOf_(rows)`, read under the lock; any RSVP, `you` or guest; Brian, Nov 9, the cap: at most one guest email per address per event; it was the RSVP's own old rows on a confirmed change only); the row still stores every typed address; an address whose rows are all gone can be mailed again; a feed without `guestLead` sends none. A failure is logged like any mail and never undoes the RSVP. Reminders stay `you`-only. The feed gains `googleCalUrl` (`googleCalUrl()` in `src/lib/events.ts`: Google's `calendar/render?action=TEMPLATE` with text, dates in UTC, details = the page, location); emails add `calendarGoogleLine` before `calendarLine`. *Confirm links (Brian, Nov 9):* `confirmLinkLine_(t, changeUrl)` builds `changeLinkLine` in the change email and `mailGuestRemove_`: its `{changeLink}` is `{ text: changeLinkWords, href: changeUrl }`, so in HTML the words `open this link` are the link and in the text the URL follows on the next line (`lineText_`); a feed without `changeLinkWords` (older than the script, `changeLinkLine` ending in `{changeUrl}`) gets the bare linked URL as before. So the script goes out before the site. *Change confirmation:* a confirmed token leaves `chgdone:<token>` (slug, submission, cells) for `CHANGE_TTL`, written inside the lock; a repeat press (the first reply can take seconds), a second tab or the link reopened shows the finished page (`donePage_`) with no second email; the confirm page's inline script locks the button on the first submit (`Confirming…`). *Failures:* an email that can't be built (a throw while building, e.g. a feed missing a field) logs `Mail: an email could not be built from the feed; nothing sent` and is skipped like a failed send: the RSVP stands, a reminder stays unstamped.
- **Mail (E7, I-087; Brian, Nov 8, 2026).** *Why:* every `MailApp.sendEmail` to an address outside the domain was rejected inside Google before it left (Admin → Email Log Search: "Delivered to an SMTP server" with no remote IP, then "Bounced: Message rejected" within 0.2 s, no bounce notice; the Sent copy to Brian arrived). Nov 8 tests from the same project to an outside address: `MailApp` plain text, with a site link, with the waiver link: all bounced; `GmailApp.sendEmail` plain text: delivered (remote IP, TLS); the full confirmation sent by hand from Gmail: delivered. So the cause is the `MailApp` path, not the content; DNS is fine (SPF `include:_spf.google.com ~all`, DKIM `google._domainkey`, DMARC `p=none`) and the Workspace is not on a trial. Why Google blocks `MailApp` here is unknown; `GmailApp` is the proven path. **`send_(ev, to, subject, mail)` is the only send point** (confirmation, can't-go, change link, spot-freed, reminder) and calls `GmailApp.sendEmail(to, subject, body, opts)` with `body` = `mail.text` and `opts = { name: sender.name, replyTo: sender.replyTo, from: <alias> }`, plus **(E13)** `htmlBody: mail.html` when the mail has one (every mail but the spot-freed note; [GmailApp.sendEmail](https://developers.google.com/apps-script/reference/gmail/gmail-app#sendEmail(String,String,String,Object)), read Nov 8, 2026: `htmlBody` "if set, devices capable of rendering HTML will use it instead of the required body argument"; the retry without `from` keeps it; no new scope) ([GmailApp.sendEmail](https://developers.google.com/apps-script/reference/gmail/gmail-app#sendEmail(String,String,String,Object)), read Nov 8, 2026: `from` "must be one of the values returned by `getAliases()`"; `name` defaults to the user's name, `replyTo` to the user's address). **The alias:** `fromAlias_(ev)` returns `sender.from` only when it equals, ignoring case, one of `GmailApp.getAliases()`; else `''` (also when `sender.from` is missing, an E6-shape feed, or `getAliases` throws). Called per send (no global memo: a reminder run sends tens, and a memo would outlive a fix to the alias). **Fallbacks, so a mail problem never undoes or blocks an RSVP:** (1) no usable alias → send without `from` (Google sends from the account's own address, the path proven on Nov 8) and `Logger.log('Mail: the events alias is not a Gmail send-as address; sent from the account address')`; (2) a send with `from` that throws → one retry without `from`, same log line; (3) a send without `from` that throws → `false`, as today (the reminder stays unstamped and goes on the next run). Logs never hold an address, a name or a subject. `MailApp.sendEmail` appears nowhere in the file. **Quota:** `MailApp.getRemainingDailyQuota()` stays as a read-only check in `remindEvent_` and `setup()` (scope `script.send_mail`, already granted; [MailApp](https://developers.google.com/apps-script/reference/mail/mail-app), read Nov 8, 2026). Google's quota page lists "Email recipients per day (for example, with MailApp)" (1,500 on Workspace) and does not say whether `GmailApp` sends lower `getRemainingDailyQuota()`; if they don't, the check is only looser, and a send refused at Google's real limit throws, so `send_` returns `false` and that reminder goes on the next run. **Scope:** `GmailApp` needs `https://mail.google.com/` (read, send and delete in Brian's whole mailbox; the GmailApp reference, read Nov 8, 2026). The manifest still has no `oauthScopes` (test 15), so Apps Script detects it from the code ([Scopes](https://developers.google.com/apps-script/concepts/scopes), read Nov 8, 2026): Brian sees a **new permission screen** when he runs `setup()` after the paste. A trigger cannot ask for consent: until it is granted, the reminder trigger fails with "Authorization is required to perform that action" (same page), so the paste, `setup()` and the consent happen in one sitting. Owner and script are in the same Workspace, so no unverified-app screen ([Client verification](https://developers.google.com/apps-script/guides/client-verification), read Nov 8, 2026). Trade-off, plainly: the script's code can now read Brian's mail; it is the repo's code, run only as Brian. A narrower `gmail.send` path (the Gmail advanced service with a hand-built MIME message and explicit `oauthScopes`) would need a manifest change and is untested against the Nov 8 block; not for this deadline. **`setup()`** also logs, for each tab whose name is a slug and whose feed loads, `From alias for <slug>: ready` or `From alias for <slug>: not a Gmail send-as address (mail goes from the account address)` or `From alias for <slug>: not in the feed yet`, never the address. **(E13)** For such a tab whose feed has no `signature`, `Signature for <slug>: not in the feed yet`; then always `Signature phone: set|not set` and `Host phone: set|not set`, never a number.
- **Quotas** (Ohm Workspace account, I-062; [Google](https://developers.google.com/apps-script/guides/services/quotas), read Nov 6, 2026): email recipients 1,500/day; triggers total runtime 6 h/day; URL Fetch 100,000/day; 30 simultaneous executions per user; 6 min per execution; 50 recipients per message (the script sends one each). From E7 the sends are `GmailApp`'s (Mail above); the recipient quota row is the same one (re-read Nov 8, 2026). Google: "additional limits apply for trial accounts" until the domain has paid at least USD 100 and 60 days have passed, so `setup()` logs the remaining quota and `sendDueReminders` stops at 0 (an unsent reminder stays unstamped and goes on the next run).

**Privacy.** Guest names and emails go only to the Apps Script and the private sheet in the Ohm Workspace account, sent by the visitor's own submit. The repo never holds guest data, the sheet ID, the script ID or a guest email (test fixtures use `example.com`). The page and the feed never show who's going: `showGoing` is `false` and has no design; the session list is always private and the page shows only spots left. No analytics, storage or URL params on event pages (the change token is in the script's URL, never the site's). **Tips are public (E6):** the status reply is open to anyone who calls the `/exec` URL, so every row in Brian's tips sheet is public the moment it is in the sheet, whether or not anyone RSVPs. Brian treats each tip as public writing: no client name or story, no contact details, no medical claim (§A6); the site's checks never see the tips. The reply carries only the tip text, never the tips sheet's ID, name, owner or any other column. **Keeping and using it** (I-066, I-065, I-069; narrowed by I-078 on Nov 7, 2026): the sheet is kept, with no deletion date. The form's promise (`rsvpText.privacy`, Brian's wording, Nov 9, 2026; was Brian's and Marea's I-078 line): "I'll use your name and email only to send event details and reminders. If you add a guest's email, I'll use it only to send them the same." It no longer mentions news and offers; the `optin` checkbox and its own `optIn` label carry that consent (RSVP form above). Two kinds of mail, two rules: (1) **event emails** for this event (confirmation, can't-go note, change link, reminder; the privacy line calls them event details and reminders) go to the RSVPer, and the spot-freed note to Brian, whatever the `Opt-in`; the script sends these and nothing else; (2) **news, offers and invitations to future events** go only to `you` rows with `Opt-in` = `yes`. An address without `yes` is never used again after this event's emails (I-069's "invitations may go to every `you` row" is withdrawn; this closes I-071 (1)). +1s (guest rows) are never contacted, except (Brian, Nov 9, 2026) the one guest email about this event when the RSVPer typed the guest's address, and the reply to an RSVP sent from that address (Changes 4, Nov 9); that address is never used for invitations or news (a guest row's `Opt-in` is always blank). Invitations and news go out from a mail tool outside this build, each with an opt-out and Ohm's postal address, opt-outs honoured within 10 business days; CAN-SPAM needs no prior consent for commercial email but "you must include the option to stop all marketing messages from you", so an opt-out from either ends both for that address (the consent rule above is Ohm's own promise, stricter than CAN-SPAM) ([FTC CAN-SPAM guide](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/can-spam-act-compliance-guide-business), read Nov 6, 2026).

- **Event-day swap (E8, I-091; Brian chose a timed deploy).** In `events.ts`: `CHAI_AT = '2026-11-22T16:00:00-07:00'` (23:00 UTC); `CHAI_NOTE: string | null = 'Chai tea led by John Marshall 🍵🫖'` (Brian, Nov 8, 2026, copy deck; the type keeps `null` as the off switch); `launchParty(limit, chaiNote = null)`: with a `chaiNote`, item 2's last note is `chaiNote` and John Marshall's role is `Chai Tea ceremony`, else the Tai Chi note and `Tai Chi instruction`; `eventsAt(nowMs) = [launchParty(SESSION_LIMIT, CHAI_NOTE !== null && nowMs >= Date.parse(CHAI_AT) ? CHAI_NOTE : null)]`; `events = eventsAt(buildNow())`, where `buildNow()` is `Date.parse(OHM_EVENTS_NOW)` when that environment variable is set (read through `globalThis.process?.env`, so the file keeps no imports; an unparseable value throws) and `Date.now()` otherwise. **All or nothing:** bullet and role swap together; setting `CHAI_NOTE` to `null` turns the whole swap off. Why build time: a static page changes only with a deploy (Brian's choice) and one clock keeps the page and the tests consistent. **Schedule:** `deploy.yml` gains `on.schedule` crons `7 23 22 11 *`, `22 23 22 11 *` and `45 23 22 11 *` (UTC: 4:07, 4:22 and 4:45 pm MST), plus a comment naming I-091. Facts ([GitHub: Events that trigger workflows → schedule](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows), read Nov 8, 2026): schedules run in UTC unless a timezone is given; "the `schedule` event can be delayed during periods of high loads" and "some queued jobs may be dropped"; they run on the latest commit of the default branch only; the shortest interval is 5 minutes; in a public repo they are disabled after 60 days without repository activity. Hence three runs, none on the hour; each rebuilds and redeploys, so a second or third run changes nothing. **Fallback** (runbook): after 4:00 pm Brian opens Actions → Deploy → Run workflow (`workflow_dispatch`, already there). **Year guard (Brian, Nov 8, 2026):** the crons would fire every Nov 22, so a first job `gate` (ubuntu, one step, `id: y`) writes `go=true` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` unless `github.event_name == 'schedule'` and `date -u +%Y` is not `2026`, then `go=false`; `build` adds `needs: gate` and `if: needs.gate.outputs.go == 'true'`; `deploy` already `needs: build`, so it is skipped with it. A push or Run workflow always deploys. Brian also has a master-list reminder to delete the schedule after the party. **Tests:** the deploy job runs `npm test` after the build, so a dist assertion about the swapped strings accepts either version but never a mix (bullet and role from the same version); unit tests pin both versions through `launchParty(n, null)`, `launchParty(n, CHAI_NOTE)` and `eventsAt` on each side of `CHAI_AT`.

Astro 7.3.5's static build writes it as `dist/launch-party.html` (`build.format: 'file'`) with `<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0;url=/events/launch-party">`, `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`, `<link rel="canonical" href="https://ohmprecisionbodywork.com/events/launch-party">` and a plain link, no script (read in `node_modules/astro/dist/core/routing/3xx.js` and `core/build/generate.js`, Nov 8, 2026; a 301 gives delay 0). `site.deploy.base` is `/`; if it ever changes, the destinations need it.
