- **RSVP result card (E9).** `ResultView` gains `answer?: Status` (absent for `pending` and the honeypot's quiet success), `statusLine?: string` (`fill(t.resultStatus, { status: t[answer] })`, I-094), `cheer?: string` (`cheerGoing` · `cheerMaybe` · `cheerCant`, I-103) and `cheerEmoji?: string` (`''` · `cheerMaybeEmoji` · `cheerCantEmoji`, I-105). Can't go now also gets these (title and text unchanged). Order inside `.rsvp-result`: H3 title · text · `p.rsvp-result__status` · `p.rsvp-result__cheer` (`<span class="rsvp-result__cheer-text">` + space + `<span class="rsvp-result__emoji" aria-hidden="true">`) · outcome lines · note · `div.rsvp-result__actions` (flex, wrap, `--s-3` gap): the calendar button, then one `<a class="btn rsvp-result__notice" target="_blank" rel="noopener">{link.label}</a>` per notice with `inResult` and a `link` (I-096; the waiver gets `inResult: true`; no new copy). The actions show exactly when `calendar` does (Going and Maybe). **After any result (I-094):** the form's `<h2>` gets `visually-hidden` (not `hidden`: the outline keeps H2 RSVP above the H3 result title; decision), `.rsvp-intro` and `.rsvp-spots` are `hidden`; the closed line is unaffected.
- **Confetti (E9, I-099; twelfth exception).** Only when `answer === 'going'` and motion is allowed. `confettiPieces(n, random)` (pure, `src/lib/rsvp.ts`): `n` pieces `{ x: −1…1, y: −1…−0.4, r: −540…540 (deg), delay: 0…150 (ms), colour: 0…3 }`. The DOM layer adds `<div class="rsvp-confetti" aria-hidden="true">` (absolute over the top centre of `.rsvp-result`, which becomes `position: relative`; `pointer-events: none`) with 24 `<i class="c{colour}">` pieces, 8×4 px rectangles, each with `--x --y --r --d` custom properties; `c0…c3` = `--accent`, `--terra-700`, `--green-700`, `--green-300`. `@keyframes ohm-confetti`: out to `(x · 10rem, y · 6rem)`, then down to `+4rem` while rotating `r`, opacity 1 → 0; 1000 ms ease-out, `animation-delay: var(--d)`, fill `forwards`. The container goes on the last `animationend` (or after 1500 ms). No library.
- **Result emoji (E9, I-105; thirteenth exception).** `.rsvp-result__emoji` is `display: inline-block`, `transform-origin: 50% 80%`. Maybe (`--maybe`): `ohm-wiggle` 1 s ease-out once: scale 0 → 1.15 → 1 by 30%, then rotate −12°, 12°, −12°, 12°, 0. Can't go (`--cant`): `ohm-droop` 1 s ease-in-out once: opacity 0 → 1 by 25%, rotate 14° and `translate: 0 2px` at 55%, back to rest. Going: no emoji (empty span). Reduced motion: shown still.
- **Tip card (E9, I-095).** `tipTitle` `Self-care tip`, `reminderTip` `Self-care tip: {tip}`. **No script paste:** the reminder line is `text.reminderTip` from the feed; `apps-script/rsvp.js` is unchanged (its only "of the day" is the comment naming Brian's sheet `Self Care tip of the day`, which keeps its name). The new words reach the Nov 21 reminder once E9 is deployed and the feed cache (600 s) turns over. **Look (the Pricing rate card's):** `background: var(--bg-dark)`, `color: var(--text-on-dark)`, `border-top: 3px solid var(--accent)`, `border-radius: var(--radius)`, `padding: var(--s-6)`, no other border; the H3 gets the rate card's `::after` rule (2px `--accent`, full width, `--s-3` above); `.rsvp-tip__next` `color: var(--text-on-dark)` (cream on green-900 10.6:1, already in `check:contrast`). **Reel (eleventh exception):** `<div class="rsvp-tip__window">` (relative, `overflow: hidden`) wraps the `aria-live` text. Each time the tip changes (first fill and `Another tip`) the DOM layer sets the real text first (the live region speaks it as before), then, if motion is allowed and there is more than one tip, adds `<div class="rsvp-tip__reel" aria-hidden="true">` (absolute, `inset: 0`, the card's background) holding a strip of `reelFor(tips, landing, random, 6)`, each item `height: var(--h)` (the window's height in px, measured after the text is set) and `overflow: hidden`; `@keyframes ohm-reel` moves the strip from `translate: 0 0` to `0 calc(-1 * var(--steps) * var(--h))` (`--steps` = items − 1), 900 ms `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.7, 0.2, 1)`, `forwards`; on `animationend` the reel goes. A click during a spin removes the reel and starts the next. `reelFor` (pure, `src/lib/rsvp.ts`): `count` items ending with `landing`; fillers come from the other tips, never equal to `landing`, and no two neighbours equal when there are three or more tips; one tip → `[landing]`. `createRsvp` exposes `allTips(): readonly string[]` (the list the deck was built from, `[]` without one).
- **Floating RSVP bar (E10, I-097).** New `RsvpBar.astro` (prop `event`; renders only with `rsvp`), placed in `events/[event].astro` straight after the hero section, so it comes early in the tab order: `<div class="rsvp-bar" role="group" aria-label={rsvpText.status} hidden>` with three `<button type="button" class="btn rsvp-bar__btn" data-status>` labelled `going`, `maybe`, `cant` (existing labels, no new copy). CSS: `position: fixed`, `inset-inline: 0`, `bottom: 0`, `z-index: 50` (under the skip link's 100), `background: var(--bg-dark)`, `border-top: 1px solid var(--green-300)`, padding `var(--s-3) var(--gutter)` with `max(var(--s-3), env(safe-area-inset-bottom))` at the bottom, buttons `flex: 1` up to 12rem, centred; no motion. `html:has(.rsvp-bar:not([hidden])) { scroll-padding-bottom: 5rem; }` so focus never lands under it (WCAG 2.4.11). Logic in `src/scripts/rsvp.ts`: visible only while not closed, no result, and the `#rsvp` section entirely below the viewport (an `IntersectionObserver` on the section; shown when it is not intersecting and its top is below the viewport). So it hides while the RSVP section is on screen **and after it** (decision: it never covers the notice, the credits or the footer). Without JS it stays hidden. A click checks `input[name="status"][value=…]`, dispatches a bubbling `change` (so the Can't go hiding runs), scrolls `#rsvp` into view (`smooth`, `auto` with reduced motion) and focuses `#rsvp-name` with `preventScroll: true`. No storage, no URL change.
- **Entrance (E10, I-098; fifteenth exception).** `class="container rise"` on each section's container after the hero in `events/[event].astro` (description and schedule, details, RSVP, notices, credits); `global.css` unchanged.
- **Timeline (E10, I-100).** Markers become 10px circles (`border-radius: 50%`; same colours, optional hollow). The line moves from the `<ol>`'s border to per-item segments: `.timeline__item::after` (2px `--line-light`, `border-left`) from its dot to the next dot, none after the last; the segment ending at an optional item is dashed (`.timeline__item:has(+ .timeline__item--optional)::after { border-left-style: dashed; }`). Text is never faded (contrast). Each `<li>` carries `data-start` and `data-end` (`end ?? next item's start ?? event.end`). Client script 6 marks the item with `start ≤ now < end` with `aria-current="time"` and `timeline__item--now` (dot 14px, `box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 30%, transparent)`; no motion), on load and every 60 s while the page is visible. Item text layout unchanged.
- **Countdown (E10, I-101).** `EventHero` adds, after `.event-when` and only when the build time is before `event.end`, `<p class="event-countdown" data-start data-end data-tz data-text={JSON of the three strings}></p>` with `min-height: calc(1em * var(--lh-body))` (no layout shift when filled), `font-weight: 600`. Client script 6 fills it: `countdown(nowMs, start, end, tz)` → `{ kind: 'days', n }` (n ≥ 2: `countdownDays`) · `{ kind: 'tomorrow' }` · `{ kind: 'today' }` (from midnight to `end`) · `null` (after `end`: empty). Days are calendar dates in `tz`, never 24-hour blocks. Without JS the line stays empty.
- **`src/lib/event-time.ts` (E10, new, pure, no imports):** `countdown` and `currentItem(items: { start: string; end: string }[], nowMs): number` (−1 when none). Kept out of `src/lib/events.ts` so client script 6 does not bundle the event data, `site.ts` or `wording.ts`.
- **Client script 6 (E10): `src/scripts/event.ts`**, imported only by `events/[event].astro`; reads the data attributes, no request, no storage. Event pages with an RSVP carry two scripts (`rsvp.ts`, `event.ts`).
- **Credit lift (E10, I-102; fourteenth exception).** `.credit`: `padding: var(--s-2)`, `margin: calc(-1 * var(--s-2))` (layout unchanged), `border-radius: var(--radius)`, `transition: translate var(--transition), box-shadow var(--transition)`; `.credit:hover, .credit:focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--shadow-lift); }`; inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` they also get `translate: 0 -2px`.
- **Sharper desktop banner (E11, I-104; Brian approved option 2 of a Code-chat preview, Nov 8, 2026; the muscle figures show only at the edges, accepted).** New `scripts/make-event-banner.mjs` (`npm run event-banner`, run by hand, sharp only) reads the committed `header-green.png` and `launch-mark-on-dark.png` (never edited) and writes into `src/assets/events/launch-party/`: (1) `banner-bg.png`, 1240×400 RGB: the banner's artwork mask (`r − g > 25` or mean > 120; its bounding box searched inside x 150–850, y 100–350), dilated 4 px, filled by normalized convolution (blur σ 6, 14, 30 of image × weight over blur of weight), cropped to the page's current view (x 190, y 125, 620×200), resized 2x (lanczos3), with a radial scrim baked in (ellipse centred on the art box, radii 0.62 and 0.78 of its width and height, opacity 0.92 at the centre, 0.85 at 70%, 0 at the edge, colour = the banner's pixel (0, 0)); (2) `banner-mark.json` `{ source, viewBox, box: { left, top, width, height } (percent of the 31:10 box, two decimals), accent, light }`: the mark (crop x 39, y 15, 694×203 of the 744×228 file) split into two layers (`r − g > 30` → accent, else light), each traced from its alpha (1 px pad, marching squares at 0.5 with the saddle rule, loops of 6 points or fewer dropped), smoothed by Chaikin twice, then simplified by Douglas–Peucker at 0.1 source px per loop (split at the point farthest from the start; a closed loop's ends coincide), one decimal, one even-odd path per layer. `box` maps the art's bounding box into the crop (`left = (x0 − 190) / 620`, …). Architect's measure, Nov 8, 2026: 23.5 KB of path data, no visible difference at 4x from the unsimplified 392 KB trace; the mark's colours are exactly `--terra-500` (195, 122, 91) and `--cream` (243, 242, 240), so the SVG fills are tokens. `graphics.wide` → `launch-party/banner-bg.png`, `graphics.wideMark` → `launch-party/banner-mark.json` (`og` stays `header-green.png`). `src/lib/event-assets.ts` adds `eventMark(path)` (an eager `import.meta.glob` of `../assets/events/**/*.json`). `EventHero`: `<div class="event-banner">` (relative) holds the `<picture>` (wide sources now `banner-bg`, widths `[620, 1240]`) and, with `wideMark`, `<svg class="event-banner__mark" viewBox preserveAspectRatio="none" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">` with `<path fill-rule="evenodd">` for each layer (`fill: var(--accent)` and `fill: var(--text-on-dark)`), absolute at the box's percentages, shown only from 48rem. From 48rem the picture keeps `aspect-ratio: 31 / 10`, `object-fit: cover`, and drops `scale: 1.6129` (the background is already that view). Below 48rem nothing changes. Budget: `banner-mark.json` ≤ 40 KB.
- **Copy (copy deck → Events):** new `rsvpText` keys `resultStatus`, `cheerGoing`, `cheerMaybe`, `cheerCant`, `cheerMaybeEmoji`, `cheerCantEmoji`, `countdownDays`, `countdownTomorrow`, `countdownToday`; changed `tipTitle`, `reminderTip`. The feed carries all of `rsvpText` as before (`v` stays 1; the script ignores keys it doesn't use).

### B11. Analytics: Umami Cloud (step A1, I-114, I-115; Brian approved the plan, Nov 8, 2026)
The third third party in the browser, after Google (Places, §B4) and the RSVP Apps Script (§B10). Spec of record: `steps/A1-analytics.md`.
- **Tag (Base, `<head>`):** `<script defer src="https://cloud.umami.is/script.js" data-website-id={analytics.websiteId} data-domains={analytics.domain}>`, values from `src/data/analytics.ts` (`websiteId` is public: it ships in every page; `domain` = `new URL(site.deploy.customDomain).hostname`, the production hostname only). No other `data-*` option. `data-domains` matches `window.location.hostname`, so localhost, `astro preview` and any other host load the script and send nothing.
- **Pinned facts** (Umami docs, read 2026-11-08): `data-domains` limits tracking to a comma-separated list matched against `window.location.hostname`; `data-exclude-search` is the opt-out for query strings, so by default pageview URLs keep them (https://docs.umami.is/docs/tracker-configuration). Payload fields: `hostname`, `language`, `referrer`, `screen`, `title`, `url`, `website` (https://docs.umami.is/docs/tracker-functions). Event names are at most 50 characters; `data-umami-event` and `umami.track()` both record events (https://docs.umami.is/docs/track-events). "Umami's web tracker does not use cookies" (https://docs.umami.is/docs/faq). Hobby (free): 100K events a month, 1 website, 6-month retention (https://umami.is/pricing).
- **What Umami receives:** pageviews (path plus query, so UTM tags on printed or social links work; the site's own links add no query) and the events below as a name plus `{ page: location.pathname }`. Never an href, a query string in event data, a form field, an address, a name or an email. No cookies, no storage.
- **Events** (`src/lib/analytics.ts`, `classifyHref` and `trackEvent`; `src/scripts/analytics.ts` is client script 7, one delegated click listener, imported only by Base): `book` (the four PocketSuite booking links, `bookingUrl` for office, central, midnorth, north), `contact` (`site.contact.lead` "Send a request" and `site.contact.chat` "Chat with me"), `email` (`mailto:`), `call` (`tel:`), `text` (`sms:`), `policies` (the client policies PDF), `rsvp` (`src/scripts/rsvp.ts`, on submit with JS on; the no-JS post sends nothing). The rules reach the browser in `<meta name="analytics-rules">`, built by Base from `site.ts`, so no link is typed in the script. `trackEvent` does nothing when `window.umami` is absent (blocked, not loaded, not production) and never throws.
- **Excluded page (I-115): `/body-map`** (health information; the page itself is planned, not built). No tag, no click script, no `analytics-rules` meta, no `data-umami*` attribute and no request to `cloud.umami.is`, in production or preview. Two locks: Base's `analytics` prop (`false` turns it off) and Base's own path opt-out (`analytics.excludedPaths`, `isExcluded`), which wins whatever a page passes; `check:dist` fails if `body-map.html` or `body-map/index.html` contains `cloud.umami.is`, `data-website-id`, `data-umami`, `analytics-rules`, the website ID or Base's click script, and passes when neither file exists.
- **`/hello` (§B8):** tracked. It carries the Umami tag and no click script (`bare` pages have no tracked links), so its one-inline-script limit is unchanged.
- **Redirect stubs** (the `/launch-party` redirect, `public/hello/index.html`): no tag; they are not built from Base.
- **Performance:** Lighthouse mobile performance on `/` and `/book` (median of 3) may drop at most 2 points from the A1 baseline.

### B12. Body map (B0–B10, I-073, I-074, I-108; spec 2026-11-07; Brian's answers Nov 8; started Nov 10, 2026)
Requirements and BM-1–BM-14: BRIEF §15. Strings: `bodymap.text` (copy deck → Body map). The full plan with reasons and rejected options is `brief/bodymap-plan_2026-11-08.md` (git-ignored); this section wins where they differ. Steps: B1 art · B2 filing script · B3 review · B4 thin slice · B5 figures and zones · B6 pins and details · B7 report and polish · B8 review · B9 verify · B10 launch.
- **Page.** `src/pages/body-map.astro` → `/body-map`; `Base bare noindex analytics={false}` (noindex always: `indexable` is already true). Not in the sitemap, not in `robots.txt`, linked from no page; `body-map` joins `RESERVED_SLUGS` (`src/lib/events.ts`); `public/body-map/index.html` refreshes `/body-map/` to `/body-map` (like `/hello`). **Not live until B10:** while `bodymap.open` is false the page shows `closed` only, with no script, no form and no endpoint URL; `OHM_BODYMAP_PREVIEW=1 npm run build` builds the real page for local and LAN-phone tests (like `OHM_EVENTS_NOW`). Needs JS; `<noscript>` shows `noscript`.
- **Art (B1, I-074).** `src/assets/bodymap/svg/<sex>_<view>.svg` and `png/<sex>_<view>.png` (2048×4096, RGB on white, used only for the PDF raster), the delivered names for `female`/`male` × `front`, `back`, `left_side`, `right_side`, plus the art's `README.md`. One viewBox `0 0 2048 4096`, groups `silhouette`, `landmarks`, `outline`. B1 strips metadata (the delivered files have none, checked Nov 10, 2026) and keeps the 887×1774 sources out of the repo (Brian's Drive has the full set). The page finds figures through one `import.meta.glob` on the folder, so a new set with the same names and viewBox needs no code change (BM-14). `female_front.svg` is 476 KB as delivered; any SVG over 400 KB after B1's cleaning (path precision first) is shown as a transparent WebP rendered from the SVG. The art's own hex fills are exempt from the no-hex rule (§D).
- **Coordinates and zoom (B4).** One `<svg viewBox>` holds the figure (`<image>`) and the pins; zoom and pan change only the `viewBox`, 1× to 6×, instantly (§A3). Taps convert through `getScreenCTM().inverse()` to 0–1 of 2048×4096 (pure, tested). Pointer events; two pointers pinch; under 8 px of movement is a tap; the wheel zooms over the figure; buttons +, −, reset. Pins keep a constant screen size (scale 1/zoom). `touch-action: none` on the figure wrapper only, the figure at most 70% of the screen height, Safari `gesturestart` prevented inside it, inputs at least 16 px.
- **Pins (B6).** `{ id, view, x, y, type, intensity: 1–5 | null, note ≤ 140, star, fromList }`; at most 60; at most 3 starred; avoid never starred (`starrable`). Shapes from `src/lib/bodymap-shapes.ts`, shared by the page and the PDF; tokens §A1. Changing the figure keeps the pins and looks the regions up again. The region list (`Prefer a list?`, one fieldset per view, head-to-toe) adds a pin of the current type at the zone's `anchor`; unticking removes only that pin. It is also the keyboard and screen-reader path.
- **Zones (B5).** `src/data/bodymap-zones/<sex>_<view>.json` per v1 figure, authored per figure, never mirrored: `{ key, anchor: [x, y], rings: [[[x, y], …]] }` in 0–1, geometry only; keys and names in `bodymap.regions` (28 front, 29 back, the same keys for both sexes). Left and right are the client's own (on a front view the client's left is the viewer's right). Point-in-polygon reuses `pointInRing` from `src/lib/geo.ts`; overlaps resolve by file order. `npm run bodymap:zones` renders overlay PNGs into `docs/build/screens/bodymap-zones/` for Brian. Zones are never drawn, and never in the HTML or the PDF.
- **Storage (B4).** One key, `ohm-bodymap-v1`: `{ v, savedAt, name, apptDate, figure, pins, id }` (`id` is `null` until the first send; Retries), written on every change inside `try/catch` (the lookup too); an entry older than 24 h or with an unknown `v` is deleted on load; cleared after a successful send and by Start over. Without storage, state stays in memory. Clock and storage are injected for tests. The note field has `autocomplete="off"`.
- **Report and PDF (B4, B7).** A small hand-written PDF writer, `src/lib/pdf.ts` (built-in Helvetica, lines, filled shapes, JPEG images; no new dependency; read back by `unpdf` in tests). Each figure is drawn once onto a canvas (about 600×1200) as a JPEG; pins are vector shapes on top. Order: header (name, appointment, sent, figure), both views with numbered pins, then `Priority` (starred), `Avoid`, `Other marks`, each line with number, type, region, `{n}/5` and note. Letters outside Latin-1 show as `?` in the PDF only. `bodymap-pdf.ts` never imports the zone files (static test); regions come from the lookup. If the writer proves fragile at B8, the architect brings jsPDF to Brian as a decision.
- **Wire contract.** One `fetch` POST to `site.bodymapUrl`, body a JSON string with no custom headers (`text/plain;charset=UTF-8`, a simple request with no preflight, as §B10): `{ v: 1, kind: 'ohm-bodymap', id: <v4 uuid, kept across retries and reloads: Retries>, website: '' (honeypot), name, apptDate: 'YYYY-MM-DD', figure, report: {…}, pdf: <base64> }`. Page caps: PDF ≤ `limits.pdfBytes` base64 characters, report ≤ `limits.reportBytes`. Replies: `{ok:true}` or `{ok:false,error:'invalid'|'busy'|'server'}`, nothing else. `busy` → `errBusy`; `invalid`/`server` → `errServer`; a network failure or a non-JSON reply → `errNetwork` with `retry`. Marks are kept until `ok`. The appointment date stays a `YYYY-MM-DD` string end to end (the page allows today −14 to +365 days; the script one more day each way, Filing script).
- **Filing script (B2).** A separate standalone project "Ohm Bodymap" in the Ohm Workspace account; source `apps-script/bodymap/bodymap.js` and `appsscript.json` (V8, `America/Denver`, `webapp { access: ANYONE_ANONYMOUS, executeAs: USER_DEPLOYING }`, `oauthScopes` exactly Drive, `exceptionLogging: NONE`). `doPost`: pause (`PAUSED` set → `busy`, Off switch) → size (over 2,000,000 characters refused before parsing) → parse → honeypot → shape (unknown keys refused) → validate (the appointment date must be a real calendar date from 15 days before to 366 days after today's Denver date: the page's window plus one day each way for a client in another time zone, I-137) → `tryLock(10000)` → idempotency (`done:<id>`) → rate limits (6 per 10 min; 30 per Denver day; 3 per `folderKey(name)` and appointment date per Denver day; stores, keys and expiry under Script state) → folder → `createFile` PDF (skipped when `pdf:<id>` is cached, Retries) then JSON → put `done:<id>`, remove `pdf:<id>`, count → release in `finally`. Any other throw (reading the cache or Script Properties) → `server`, logged `bodymap: state-error`. `doGet` always replies `invalid` and touches nothing. Folder: Script Property `CLIENTS_FOLDER_ID` (Brian types it in the editor, never the repo or chat, I-075); exactly one subfolder not in the trash whose `folderKey` equals the typed name's → there. A subfolder in the trash is skipped: it never receives a map and doesn't count toward "several" (I-137). A name whose `folderKey` is empty matches no folder. None or several → `_Unsorted_Intakes`, the first subfolder of that name not in the trash. When there is none, the send makes it again (`createFolder`) and logs nothing extra (I-137). `setup()` only makes it ahead of time and says which happened. File names: `<apptDate> Body map, <Name> (sent <yyyy-MM-dd HH.mm>)` `.pdf` and `.json`, the name stripped of `/\:*?"<>|` and control characters, at most 60 characters. Logs: `console.warn` with fixed codes only, one per refusal or fault (I-128): `bodymap: paused`, `bodymap: invalid` (size, parse, honeypot, shape or validation), `bodymap: busy-lock`, `bodymap: busy-window`, `bodymap: busy-day`, `bodymap: busy-name`, `bodymap: drive-error`, `bodymap: state-error`; `setup()` logs only `bodymap: reachable`, `bodymap: unsorted-created` or `bodymap: unsorted-found`. Executions doesn't show the web app's log lines (Pinned facts), so the codes are for the code, the tests and editor runs. Brian reads a client send's outcome from Script Properties (`PAUSED`, `DAY_COUNTS`) and run durations (runbook parts 7 and 12). No email (Brian, Nov 8, 2026), and no Drive deletion. The only removal is the script's own cache entry `pdf:<id>`. **Write-only** is a code promise (the script runs as Brian): a static ban on read, share and fetch APIs, fixed replies, read-style requests getting the generic reply, and live `curl` checks at B2 and B9.
- **Script state (B2, I-126).** Everything the script keeps outside Drive, read and written only while it holds the lock (except `PAUSED`, read first). Validation refuses (`invalid`) an `id` that isn't a lower-case version-4 UUID (`^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$`, 36 characters), so a key holds only that random id, never typed text, and stays far under 250 characters.
  - **Pause switch (I-128):** Script Property `PAUSED`, set and deleted only by Brian by hand; the script only reads it (Off switch).
  - **Done marker:** script cache (CacheService), key `done:<id>`, value `1`, expiry 21,600 s.
  - **PDF-filed marker (I-127):** script cache, key `pdf:<id>`, value the send's epoch ms as a decimal string, expiry 21,600 s. It is removed (`cache.remove`) once both files exist, right after `done:<id>` is put, so it only links a filed PDF to its missing JSON (I-137). A throw putting or removing it is a `state-error` fault.
  - **10-minute window:** script cache, key `win`, value `<count>:<t0>` (`t0` = epoch ms of the window's first counted send), expiry `max(1, ceil(600 − (now − t0) / 1000))` s, so the window closes 600 s after `t0` (the pattern of `allowMail_` in `apps-script/rsvp.js`).
  - **Denver-day and per-name counts:** Script Properties (PropertiesService), one property `DAY_COUNTS`, value JSON `{"d":"<yyyy-MM-dd>","n":<count>,"k":{"<nameKey>":<count>}}`, where `d` is the send day, `Utilities.formatDate(new Date(), 'America/Denver', 'yyyy-MM-dd')`. No expiry: a missing or unparseable value, or a `d` that isn't today, reads as `{d: today, n: 0, k: {}}`, so both counts reset by themselves at the first send after Denver midnight (and when Brian deletes the property by hand). `k` gains one entry per counted send, so at most 30 (about 1 KB, under the 9 KB value limit).
  - **`nameKey`:** the first 16 hex characters of `Utilities.computeDigest(Utilities.DigestAlgorithm.SHA_256, folderKey(name) + '|' + apptDate, Utilities.Charset.UTF_8)`, each byte as two lower-case hex digits of `b & 255` (so it is right whether the bytes come back signed or not). For `Test Client` on `2026-12-03` the input is `test client|2026-12-03`. "3 per name and date per day" means: at most 3 counted sends a Denver day whose typed names share a `folderKey` and whose `apptDate` (the appointment date, not the send day) is the same; the same name with another appointment date has its own count. **No salt:** Script Properties are seen only in the project's settings and the cache only by the project's code, and anyone with that access can already run code as Brian with Drive scope and open the filed maps, so a salt would add a secret to manage and protect nothing.
  - **Checks and counting:** step 8 replies `busy` when the `win` count ≥ `rate.perTenMinutes`, `n` ≥ `rate.perDay` or `k[nameKey]` ≥ `rate.perNameAndDatePerDay` (the script's copies of `bodymap.rate`, kept equal by a test). Step 11, only after both files exist, adds 1 to each (a missing `win` starts a window with `t0` = now). A refused, `invalid`, `server` or replayed (`done:`) send counts nothing.
  - **Early eviction** (the cache "may be removed before" its expiry, Pinned facts): a lost `done:<id>` or `pdf:<id>` lets a retry with that `id` file a second copy (Retries); a lost `win` restarts the window, so up to 6 more may pass inside those 10 minutes (the limit loosens; it never blocks a real client). Script Properties have no documented expiry, so the day and per-name counts hold until Denver midnight.
- **Retries and partial writes (B2, B4, I-127).** **Page:** the `id` is a lower-case version-4 UUID built from `crypto.getRandomValues` (`crypto.randomUUID` is secure-context only, and the LAN preview is plain http). It is made at the first send and kept in memory and in the storage entry across retries and reloads; it is dropped on `ok`, on Start over, with the 24 h entry, and on any change to the name, date, figure or pins, so a retry always carries what was first sent under that `id` and an edit is never swallowed by `done:<id>`. **Script:** as soon as the PDF's `createFile` returns, it puts `pdf:<id>`; the sent stamp in both file names comes from `pdf:<id>` when it is cached, else from now. Once both files exist, it puts `done:<id>`, removes `pdf:<id>` and adds to the counts, and the reply is `ok`. A throw in any of these is logged `bodymap: state-error` and changes nothing else. The sequences, each a retry with the same `id`:
  - **(a)** PDF written, the JSON `createFile` throws → `server` (lock released, nothing counted, no `done:`). The retry: no `done:` → limits → folder → `pdf:<id>` cached, so it writes the JSON only, named with the PDF's stamp → `done:`, count, `ok`. One pair.
  - **(b)** Both files written, the reply is lost; the retry inside 6 h finds `done:<id>` → `ok`, no Drive call, nothing counted, even when a limit is now full (idempotency runs before the limits).
  - **(c)** As (b), but `done:<id>` has expired or been evicted → a second full pair with a later stamp, counted again. `pdf:<id>` was removed when the first pair was filed, so the retry can't take (a)'s JSON-only path, which would add a second JSON with the first pair's name (I-137). That happens only if the removal also threw (`state-error`) and the marker is still cached. Likewise (a) with `pdf:<id>` gone → the lone PDF stays and a full pair follows.
  - **Why a marker:** `pdf:<id>` is one cache write and one cache removal (no Drive read, no Drive delete, nothing on the static ban list), and when it is evicted the result is only the duplicate that having no marker would always give.
  - **Accepted result:** when a marker is gone the script can't tell, so Drive holds two copies of one send with the same marks (two pairs, or a lone PDF and a later pair; after a failed removal, a second JSON beside the first pair). Brian keeps the later pair and deletes the rest by hand (runbook part 6). The page keeps an `id` up to 24 h and the markers last at most 6 h, so (c) needs a retry more than 6 h after the first try, or an eviction.
- **Deploy (B2).** Through E16's `scripts/push-apps-script.mjs`, which stages only the files of one target in a fresh `.apps-script-build/`, so neither project can receive the other's files (I-109, checked at B0: lines 16–21 copy `rsvp.js` and `appsscript.json` only). B2 adds a `bodymap` target and a `bodymap` entry in the gitignored `.apps-script-ids.json`; the `/exec` URL goes in `site.bodymapUrl` (public by design, like `rsvpUrl`), and the Script ID and folder ID never go in the repo. **The URL is public from B2, not B10** (`site.ts` is in a public repo, though the closed page doesn't ship it), so anyone can file a well-formed map under any client's name (only the PDF's magic bytes are checked) or spend the day's 30 sends so real clients get `busy`; accepted because the script can only create files and never returns Drive data, each name and appointment date is capped at 3 a day, a filed map is unverified until the client confirms it, and Brian can pause filing in seconds, so the worst case is clutter in Drive and a busy day, never a leak.
- **Off switch (B2, I-128).** While the Script Property `PAUSED` holds any non-empty value, `doPost` replies `busy` before the size check and logs `bodymap: paused`, touching nothing else (no parse, lock, cache, counts or Drive); `doGet` is unchanged. Brian sets `PAUSED` = `1`, or deletes it, in the editor's Project Settings → Script Properties: no push, version or deployment. Assumed, and checked live at B2: the next request reads the new value. Meanwhile clients see `errBusy` and keep their marks. **Rotating the URL** (runbook part 8, only if the URL itself is targeted): keep `PAUSED` set; Deploy → New deployment (Web app, Execute as Me, Anyone) gives a new `/exec` URL; an Item sets `site.bodymapUrl` and the site deploys; archive the old deployment in Manage deployments; a `curl` GET of the old URL must no longer return `{"ok":false,"error":"invalid"}` (Google doesn't document what an archived URL returns; if it still answers, keep `PAUSED` and raise an Item); then delete `PAUSED`. A new URL is public again once committed, so rotation only shakes off whoever saved the old one. After B10, `bodymap.open: false` (an Item and a site deploy) also closes the page itself.
- **Privacy.** Health information is only in page memory, `localStorage` (≤ 24 h), the HTTPS POST body and Drive. Never in the repo or `dist/`, console logs (page or script), analytics (none on this page, §B11), URLs or titles, a script reply or log line, a cache key or value, a Script Property name or value (the per-name count is keyed by a digest, Script state; `DAY_COUNTS` holds only the send day), or a Drive file name beyond name and dates. Fixtures use fake names (`Test Client`, `Alex Example`, `Sam Sample`) and `fake note`. B8 runs the AC-12 greps listed in the plan's section 6; the first three join `check:secrets` in B2.
- **Checks added by later steps.** `check:dist` (B4, B7): `body-map.html` noindex with a self canonical, not in the sitemap or `robots.txt`, no inbound links, exactly one script while open (none while closed), no zone markup, same-origin `src`/`href`, the JS chunk names no host but the site, `script.google.com` and `www.w3.org`. `check:wording` (B4): the page is exempt from the credential rule (bare) and always fails on the licensure words. `check:secrets` (B2): Drive folder URLs, script editor URLs, a `"scriptId"` key, `.clasp.json` names. `check:contrast` (B1): the pin rules in §A1. `tests/page-transition.test.ts` pins `body-map.html` at 0 scripts while closed and 1 while open. `npm run e2e:bodymap` (local, Playwright; CI has no browsers).
- **Pinned facts** (read 2026-11-10 unless noted). Apps Script quotas, Workspace: 6 min per execution, 30 simultaneous executions per user, Properties 500,000 reads/writes a day, 9 KB per value, 500 KB per store; no documented limit on incoming web-app request size (https://developers.google.com/apps-script/guides/services/quotas). CacheService: keys at most 250 characters, at most 100 KB per key, expiry 1 s to 21,600 s (6 h), "cached data may be removed before this time" (https://developers.google.com/apps-script/reference/cache/cache). `Utilities.computeDigest(algorithm, value, charset)` digests a `String` in the given character set and returns `Byte[]`; `DigestAlgorithm` includes `SHA_256`; `Charset` is `US_ASCII` or `UTF_8`; `formatDate(date, timeZone, format)` follows Java's `SimpleDateFormat` (https://developers.google.com/apps-script/reference/utilities/utilities, https://developers.google.com/apps-script/reference/utilities/digest-algorithm, https://developers.google.com/apps-script/reference/utilities/charset; I-126). Web apps: `doPost(e)` gets the body in `e.postData.contents` and its MIME type in `e.postData.type`; the page states no size limit and doesn't cover CORS; a web app is deployed with Deploy > New deployment > Web app (https://developers.google.com/apps-script/guides/web). Manifest `webapp.access`: `ANYONE_ANONYMOUS` is "Any user, even if not logged in", `MYSELF` "Only the deploying user can run the app" (https://developers.google.com/apps-script/manifest/web-app-api-executable). Deployments: "To deploy a change to the project code, create a new version and edit the deployment to use it", which keeps "the same URL or deployment ID"; "You can't delete versioned deployments … Instead, you can archive them"; "Deployment IDs only appear on active deployments"; the page doesn't say what an archived deployment's URL returns (https://developers.google.com/apps-script/concepts/deployments). Script Properties: "Manually add up to fifty custom properties … from the project settings page", where they can be edited and deleted; no expiry is stated (https://developers.google.com/apps-script/guides/properties). The My Executions panel lists executions, including type "Webapp", with start time, duration and status; Cloud logs (`console.*`) "persist for many days", with "a simplified version of these logs in the Apps Script dashboard"; neither page says how an anonymous web app's `console` output is shown (https://developers.google.com/apps-script/guides/dashboard, https://developers.google.com/apps-script/guides/logging; I-128). Observed in B2's live check (Nov 10, 2026; I-137): Executions lists the web app's runs (type Web App, start time, duration, status), but the rows don't open to show log lines. The codes show only for runs from the editor, such as `setup()`. So no runbook step or review check depends on reading a client send's log line. Making those lines visible (runbook part 12) is a decision for Brian and isn't built. `crypto.randomUUID()` "is available only in secure contexts (HTTPS), in some or all supporting browsers" (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Crypto/randomUUID); "`getRandomValues()` is the only member of the `Crypto` interface which can be used from an insecure context" (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Crypto/getRandomValues; I-127). `touch-action: none` stops the browser's own panning and zooming on that element (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/touch-action, read 2026-11-08). Apps Script and Drive are on Google's HIPAA-covered list for Workspace (https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/security/compliance/hipaa, updated 2026-10-28, read 2026-11-08); the BAA is Brian's (BRIEF §15).

## D. Stack rules (method v3.2, static-site profile)

Each rule is marked **check** (enforced by `npm run check`) or **convention** (checked at review). A convention gets a check only after it has been broken twice.

- **convention** Events (§B10, I-048–I-050): an event is a data entry, never new code. RSVP data (name, email, guests) goes only to the Apps Script at `site.rsvpUrl`, by the visitor's own submit; the repo never holds guest data, the sheet ID, the script ID or a real guest email; replies never carry emails, names or the guest list. `apps-script/rsvp.js` reads event facts from the site's feed, so it holds none. From E2 there are five client scripts: the four below plus `src/scripts/rsvp.ts`, imported only by `RsvpForm` (event pages with RSVP; `launch-party.html` carries one script). From E10 six: plus `src/scripts/event.ts` (countdown and the timeline's current item), imported only by `events/[event].astro`; `events/launch-party.html` carries two, and the `/launch-party` redirect page none (E8). From A1 (§B11) seven: plus `src/scripts/analytics.ts`, imported only by Base on every page except `bare` pages and `/body-map`; every page built from Base also carries the third-party Umami tag (not counted as a client script), so the per-page script counts in the tests rise accordingly. From B4 (§B12) eight: plus `src/scripts/bodymap.ts`, imported only by `body-map.astro` and only while `bodymap.open` is true or `OHM_BODYMAP_PREVIEW=1`.
- **convention** Body map (§B12, I-073): the second Apps Script exception. Map data goes only to `site.bodymapUrl`, by the client's own send; the filing script only creates files, and its replies, logs, cache and Script Properties carry no name, appointment date, folder or file ID. `/body-map` is the one page that needs JavaScript (a `<noscript>` line says so). The art under `src/assets/bodymap/` keeps its own hex fills (images, exempt from the no-hex rule); page and PDF colours come from the §A1 pin tokens. No health information in the repo, `dist/`, logs, URLs, analytics or file names beyond name and dates.
- **convention** Astro, static output, TypeScript strict. No JavaScript except where a feature needs it (§B4 booking router and deferred terrain, §B8 `/hello`, §B9 `/client-policies`, §B3 `Header` Home logo spin, §B10 the RSVP form, §B11 analytics). Four client scripts before E2: `src/scripts/book.ts` (imported only by `book/index.astro`), `src/scripts/policies.ts` (step 14, imported only by `client-policies.astro`), `src/scripts/logo-spin.ts` (step V, imported only by `index.astro`) and `src/scripts/terrain.ts` (I-054, imported only by `ServiceMap.astro`, so it is on `/book` and on each `/book/[zone]` page). `book.html` carries three scripts and each zone page one (the terrain loader; before I-054 the zone pages had none). Each page works with JS off (the maps then have no terrain). (`check:dist` checks scripts on `hello.html` only; script placement elsewhere is checked at review, by `tests/logo-spin.test.ts`, `tests/terrain-defer.test.ts`, and from M1 by `tests/page-transition.test.ts`, which pins every built page's script count.)
- **convention** Motion (§A3 fifth to tenth exceptions, M1 and M2; Brian, Oct 30 2026) is CSS only: page transitions are the browser's native cross-document view transitions (`@view-transition`), never Astro's `ClientRouter` (it ships a client router and breaks the zero-JS rule); scroll effects use `animation-timeline` and `animation-trigger` behind `@supports`, with the static design as the fallback. No motion library.
- **convention** CSS is inlined (I-053, Nov 5 2026): `astro.config.mjs` sets `build.inlineStylesheets: 'always'` (Astro docs, https://docs.astro.build/en/reference/configuration-reference/#buildinlinestylesheets, read 2026-11-05: project styles always go in `<style>` tags), so `dist/` has no `_astro/*.css` and no `<link rel="stylesheet">`; nothing blocks first paint on a CSS request. Tests that read a page's CSS take inline `<style>` blocks and any linked file, so they hold either way. Keep `build.format: 'file'` beside it.
- **convention** GitHub Pages via `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`; every push to `main` deploys production at `https://ohmprecisionbodywork.com` (`chimpanbeat.github.io/ohm-site` 301s there). The custom domain was cut over on Nov 6, 2026 (I-018). Nothing reaches production without Brian.
- **convention** Single sources: business facts in `src/data/site.ts`, wording in `src/data/wording.ts`, tokens in `src/styles/tokens.css`, copy in `docs/build/copy-deck.md`. No page hardcodes a rate, day, link or zone name; no raw hex outside `tokens.css`.
- **convention** Contract files are listed in `.claude/hooks/protected.json`; only the architect, or a step file that lists them under `## Files`, changes them. `geo.ts` bodies may change, never its exported names or types.
- **convention** `noindex` until launch: `indexable` in `site.ts` is `site.licensed && site.deploy.live`, and the launch sets `deploy.live`.
- **check** `check:wording`: licensure wording rules (BRIEF §7) on the built HTML.
- **check** `check:contrast`: every text/background token pair meets WCAG AA.
- **check** `check:dist`: titles, descriptions, canonicals, noindex, inline-script, (A1) analytics-tag and (Nov 9, 2026) outbound-link rules on the built HTML (§B5, §B11).
- **check** Outbound links open in a new tab (`check:dist`, Brian, Nov 9 2026): on every built page, every `<a>` whose `href` is `http(s)://` on another host carries `target="_blank"` and a `rel` containing `noopener` (never `noreferrer` alone: PocketSuite and John-Mark may want the referrer). Not outbound: the site's own host (`site.url`), any `*.github.io` host, `mailto:`, `tel:` and relative links. **convention** with it: buttons and standalone links (PocketSuite booking buttons in `OfficeCard` and `ZoneCard`, `Send a request` / `Chat with me` in `ContactButtons` and the `/book` boundary line, the OpenStreetMap credit, the footer brand credit) end with `<span class="visually-hidden"> (opens in a new tab)</span>`; inline links inside a client-policies sentence don't (a test compares the sentence text), and `client-policies.astro` adds `target`/`rel` to any non-own-host `href` in the policy text.
- **check** `check:secrets` (`tools/check-secrets.mjs`): no credential files, keys, tokens, email addresses or (E13) phone numbers in git (US formats with separators, and `tel:`/`sms:` links; the fictional 555-0100 to 555-0199 range is allowed for tests). The public business address carries `secrets-scan: allow`; a line with that marker is skipped for every pattern.
- **check** `npm test`: routing, zones, geometry, map and script tests.
- **check** Lighthouse mobile ≥ 90 in all four categories on the key pages, at the pre-launch review (AC-5).
- **convention** Evidence: `npm run shots` captures every built route at 375 and 1280 px into `docs/build/screens/` (gitignored); every AC is covered by a test or a named screenshot. From M1 it captures with `reducedMotion: 'reduce'`, so screens show the settled static design (motion is checked in the step's browser checks).
- **convention** Public repo: never commit `.env`, the KML, client data, anything under `brief/` except `BRIEF.md`, the office street address, business-plan financials or PocketSuite admin details.
- **convention** The visitor's address never leaves the browser except in the Google request: no logging, no storage, no URL params, no analytics.
- **convention** Analytics (§B11, A1, I-114): Umami Cloud only, the tag from `src/data/analytics.ts` with `data-domains` set to the production hostname only; no cookies, no storage. Umami receives pageviews and event names with the page path only: never hrefs, query strings in event data, form contents or the address. No other analytics or tag manager without Brian's OK.
- **check** Analytics tag (`check:dist`, A1): every page built from Base except `/body-map` carries the Umami tag once, with `data-website-id` and `data-domains` equal to the production hostname.
- **check** `/body-map` loads no analytics (`check:dist`, I-115): fails if `body-map.html` or `body-map/index.html` contains `cloud.umami.is`, `data-website-id`, `data-umami`, `analytics-rules` or Base's click script; passes when the page doesn't exist.
- **convention** Unknown facts become `TODO(Brian):` comments plus an open todo in the master list. Never invent facts, copy claims, testimonials or credentials. New dependencies need Brian's OK.
